items.prompt:
Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Light tells the story: a few strong sources — crystals and cracks that glow from within — throw colored light upward, the light comes from below. Cold and warm light contrast. Dust motes and grains of sand float in the light. Moderate detail, clean readable forms. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime. Match the brushwork, lighting and color handling of the attached style reference images, but do NOT copy their subjects, objects, letters or composition.

Format: game UI icon, square. One bold emblem, centered, about 80% of the canvas, frontal view, a simple strong silhouette that stays readable at 24 px, crisp clean edges, painted material detail inside the silhouette. The glow stays inside the shape: no halo outside the silhouette.

Subject: 'Rune of Valor', the emblem of a hero's valor. A thick rounded-hexagon tablet of dark basalt with a bevelled rim of old gold; carved deep into its face is a five-pointed star made of angular rune strokes, glowing warm gold (#DDBC7A) from within; hairline cracks in the stone leak the same golden light. Frontal, symmetric, heavy and precious.

Isolate the subject on a perfectly flat, uniform, solid pure magenta background (#FF00FF) that fills the whole canvas edge to edge: no gradient, no vignette, no texture, no floor, no cast shadow, no reflection, no glow or light spill on the background, no checkerboard transparency pattern. Leave a clear margin of background around the subject. Do not use magenta or similar colors anywhere in the subject.

No text, no letters, no numbers, no real-world alphabets, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no border or frame around the picture.

items.title: Арена боя · Мастерская форм, вид сверху
items.source: docs/gdd/08-биомы.md §8.5; docs/lore/мастерская-форм-текст.md, с. 2; docs/lore/дайджест.md «Мотивы и палитра»
items.prompt:
Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Light tells the story: a few strong sources — crystals and cracks that glow from within — throw colored light upward, the light comes from below. Cold and warm light contrast. Dust motes and grains of sand float in the light. Moderate detail, clean readable forms. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime. Match the brushwork, lighting and color handling of the attached style reference images, but do NOT copy their subjects, objects, letters or composition.

Format: vertical battle background for a phone screen, portrait 9:16. Strict top-down orthographic view, the camera looks straight down at the floor like a tabletop RPG battle map: no horizon, no perspective walls, no ceiling, no sky. The central area stays open, calm and lower in contrast: two teams of five cards will stand on it, heroes in the lower third and enemies in the upper third. Put the interesting details along the edges and in the corners. Even, readable lighting over the playfield, no strong hotspot in the center.

Subject: the floor of the Workshop of Forms, the first hall under the city of Endalor, where a god once sculpted living beings from clay and abandoned the work halfway. Large worn stone floor slabs with cracks; drifts and still ripples of pale sand everywhere; in the cracks grow white-green crystals glowing from within, their cold light pooling on the floor. Two or three columns of sand seen from above: thin streams fall from the unseen vault into round conical piles with a soft haze around them. Along the left and right edges: parts of heavy wooden worktables seen from above with unfinished clay works lying on them — a hand without fingers, a face without features, half of a small beast — sculpting chisels, clay-stained cloths, clay pots. At the very top and bottom edges: the foot of the stone walls with half-formed clay bodies emerging from the stone, made precisely and calmly, unfinished, not grotesque. Colors: near-black stone, cold white-green crystal light, pale sand, warm ochre clay as the only warm accent. No grid, no characters on the playfield.

No text, no letters, no numbers, no real-world alphabets, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no border or frame around the picture.
items.status: заменён: в первом промте Lite нарисовал слоты карт, Pro сделал зал тёплым; промт исправлен

items.prompt:
Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Light tells the story: a few strong sources — crystals and cracks that glow from within — throw colored light upward, the light comes from below. Cold and warm light contrast. Format: vertical hero card portrait, 4:5. Half-body, three-quarter view, head in the upper third, face well lit and readable at small size; the lower quarter may be darker because the card puts the name there. Rich atmospheric background that tells where the hero lived, with depth and soft focus, darker than the character. Light comes from below and from glowing crystals; rim light separates the figure from the background.

Subject: Ilmerra, an elven woman from long ago, keeper of a hall where the hourglasses of those who had no kin were kept; a healer of the Air school. Ageless calm face with the fine lines of great age, gentle and attentive, long silver-white hair loosely braided with thin leather cords, pointed elven ears. She holds a small old hourglass with scratched glass close to her ear and listens to the sand inside, eyes half-closed. Layered druid robes of muted sage-green and grey linen, a woven shawl, a simple necklace of wooden beads; faint white-green wisps of wind curl around her sleeves (Air school). Background: a vast quiet hall among colossal tree roots in the heart of the elven forest; in niches between the roots stand rows of hourglasses, each one slightly different, dim; soft white-green light rises from below, sand motes drift in the air. She is lit from below by that white-green light, with a subtle rim light on her hair.

No text, no letters, no numbers, no real-world alphabets, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no border or frame around the picture.

items.title: Арена боя · Мастерская форм, вид сверху
items.source: docs/gdd/08-биомы.md §8.5; docs/lore/мастерская-форм-текст.md, с. 2; docs/lore/дайджест.md «Мотивы и палитра»
items.prompt:
Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Light tells the story: a few strong sources — crystals and cracks that glow from within — throw colored light upward, the light comes from below. Cold and warm light contrast. Dust motes and grains of sand float in the light. Moderate detail, clean readable forms. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime. Match the brushwork, lighting and color handling of the attached style reference images, but do NOT copy their subjects, objects, letters or composition.

Format: vertical battle background for a phone screen, portrait 9:16. Strict top-down orthographic view, the camera looks straight down at the floor like a tabletop RPG battle map: no horizon, no perspective walls, no ceiling, no sky. The central playfield — the middle 60% of the width, from 15% to 85% of the height — is plain floor only: stone slabs, sand ripples and fine cracks, calm and lower in contrast. No crystals, objects, markings, slots, frames, rectangles, cards, tokens or figures on the playfield: the game places its own pieces there later. Put the interesting details along the edges and in the corners. Even, readable lighting over the playfield, no strong hotspot in the center.

Subject: the floor of the Workshop of Forms, the first hall under the city of Endalor, where a god once sculpted living beings from clay and abandoned the work halfway. Large worn stone floor slabs with cracks; drifts and still ripples of pale sand. White-green crystals glowing from within grow only in the cracks along the edges and in the corners; their cold light spills onto the floor. In the corners: thin streams of sand fall from the unseen vault into small round piles with a faint haze, like hourglasses nobody turns. Along the left and right edges: parts of heavy wooden worktables seen from above with unfinished clay works lying on them — a hand without fingers, a face without features, half of a small beast — sculpting chisels, clay-stained cloths, clay pots. At the very top and bottom edges: the foot of the stone walls with half-formed clay bodies emerging from the stone, made precisely and calmly, unfinished, not grotesque. The hall is cold: near-black stone, white-green crystal light, pale sand. The only warm color is the ochre clay of the unfinished works. No candles, no fire, no warm lamps, no grid, no characters.

No text, no letters, no numbers, no real-world alphabets, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no border or frame around the picture.

items.title: Безликий образец — рядовой, сила
items.source: docs/lore/мастерская-форм-текст.md, с. 5
items.prompt:
Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Light tells the story: a few strong sources — crystals and cracks that glow from within — throw colored light upward, the light comes from below. Dust motes and grains of sand float in the light. Moderate detail, clean readable forms. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime. Match the brushwork, lighting and color handling of the attached style reference images: the first shows how we paint characters, the second shows the Workshop's clay and its cold white-green crystal light. Do NOT copy their subjects or composition.

Format: vertical enemy card portrait, 4:5, shown small on the battle field (about 74 px wide) and large in the bestiary. Three-quarter view, the figure fills most of the frame, head and shoulders in the upper third, clear readable silhouette. This is a NEW ORIGINAL design made from the description only. World rule: every creature of the Workshop of Forms was sculpted of clay by a god and left unfinished — the 'samples' are rough unfinished tries, each named after its missing or unfinished part; the 'servants' are more finished, with even hands, faces, aprons and tools; the Master is the only finished one, smooth and polished. Everything is made precisely and calmly — unfinished, but not ugly and not grotesque. Clay colors: grey-green and warm ochre, visible finger marks and tool strokes on the clay. Figures have elven proportions unless the description says otherwise. Background: the dim abandoned Workshop of Forms deep underground — dark stone, a thin stream of sand falling from a crack above, white-green crystals glowing from within in the cracks; darker and softer than the figure. The whole scene is lit by cold white-green crystal light from below; no red, orange or warm light; the clay is the only warm color. All fourteen creatures of this set share the same painting style, palette and lighting.

Subject: 'Faceless Sample', the first creature anyone meets in the Workshop. An elven figure of grey-green clay in a rough sketch of clothing, with a rope instead of a belt, holding a stone blank of a sword that has no crossguard yet. No face at all — only two shallow dents pressed by a thumb where the eyes should be; still it looks straight at the viewer. Made simply but solidly, honest, walks straight at you.

No text, no letters, no numbers, no runes that look like letters, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no border or frame around the picture. No gore, no blood, no horror grotesque.

items.title: Упор — элита, держит удар
items.source: docs/lore/мастерская-форм-текст.md, с. 14
items.prompt:
Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Light tells the story: a few strong sources — crystals and cracks that glow from within — throw colored light upward, the light comes from below. Dust motes and grains of sand float in the light. Moderate detail, clean readable forms. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime. Match the brushwork, lighting and color handling of the attached style reference images: the first shows how we paint characters, the second shows the Workshop's clay and its cold white-green crystal light. Do NOT copy their subjects or composition.

Format: vertical enemy card portrait, 4:5, shown small on the battle field (about 74 px wide) and large in the bestiary. Three-quarter view, the figure fills most of the frame, head and shoulders in the upper third, clear readable silhouette. This is a NEW ORIGINAL design made from the description only. World rule: every creature of the Workshop of Forms was sculpted of clay by a god and left unfinished — the 'samples' are rough unfinished tries, each named after its missing or unfinished part; the 'servants' are more finished, with even hands, faces, aprons and tools; the Master is the only finished one, smooth and polished. Everything is made precisely and calmly — unfinished, but not ugly and not grotesque. Clay colors: grey-green and warm ochre, visible finger marks and tool strokes on the clay. Figures have elven proportions unless the description says otherwise. Background: the dim abandoned Workshop of Forms deep underground — dark stone, a thin stream of sand falling from a crack above, white-green crystals glowing from within in the cracks; darker and softer than the figure. The whole scene is lit by cold white-green crystal light from below; no red, orange or warm light; the clay is the only warm color. All fourteen creatures of this set share the same painting style, palette and lighting. Every creature is made entirely of clay: a matte clay surface with finger marks, seams and tool strokes; no human skin, no realistic flesh; hair is sculpted clay; eyes are pressed hollows or smooth clay without pupils. They must not look like living people, orcs or goblins.

Subject: 'Prop', a servant of the Workshop: on servants like him the work was held in place while the clay set, and nobody has ever managed to move him. A broad, squat, immovable elf of grey-green clay with warm ochre patches — wide as a door, a thick neck, heavy shoulders, pointed elven ears, a calm stubborn face with pressed eyes. A clay apron, forearms bound in cloth wraps. items.title: Арена Эхо: Иш-Кантун, неделя эльфов — 21:9, одна сцена без перехода
items.source: ADR-0025, п. 8; ADR-0024; docs/content/герои/состав-героев.md, «Эльфы — Иш-Кантун»; раскладка — jobs/arena-02.json
items.prompt:
Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Light tells the story: a few strong sources — cracks and jade inlays in old stone that glow from within — throw colored light upward, the light comes from below. Cold and warm light contrast. Dust motes, pollen and tiny sparks float in the light. Moderate detail, clean readable forms. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime, no cartoon.

Format: wide horizontal battle background for a landscape phone screen, 21:9. Strict top-down orthographic view, the camera looks straight down at the ground like a tabletop RPG battle map: no horizon, no perspective, no side view of buildings, no sky. The attached image is our battle arena of a different place, the Workshop of Forms: take from it ONLY the straight-down camera, the scale, the layout of the zones and the painting style. Do NOT copy its objects, materials or colors: no worktables, no clay figures, no crystals, no sand. The game puts its cards along the left and right sides: five hero cards in the left quarter and five enemy cards in the right quarter, from the top edge to the bottom edge. So the left quarter (0-25% of the width) and the right quarter (75-100% of the width) must be open, flat, evenly lit ground over their whole height: plaza slabs, moss in the seams and fine cracks only — no steps, no walls, no statues, no bowls, no plants, no objects there. Unlike our biome arenas, this arena is a single scene: the fight begins and ends here, the camera never moves on to a next room, so nothing in the picture leads onward — no doorway, no road, no stairway, no passage out of the picture. The forest appears only as a thin dark strip along the very top and bottom edges, no more than 7% of the height. All details are placed only in the central half (25-75% of the width), close to the top and bottom edges; the middle of the central half stays calm and open, because the game shows banners there.

Subject: the great plaza of Ish-Kantun at night, at the foot of a jade stepped pyramid deep in an ancient forest, seen straight from above — the one place where the whole fight happens. Ground: large worn slabs of pale grey stone with a faint jade tint, tightly fitted, some lifted and cracked by roots; dark moss in the seams, a few fallen leaves and scattered green feathers; thin cracks glow from within with cold jade-green light. In the central half only: along the top edge, the lowest tiers of a jade-green stepped pyramid seen straight from above — straight parallel step edges running across the central half, cut off by the top edge of the picture; along the bottom edge, a great round stone calendar disc set flat into the plaza, seen straight from above, only its upper half visible, carved with concentric rings of abstract ornament — notches, spirals, feather and jaguar-spot patterns, nothing like writing or numbers — with jade-green light glowing in its grooves; near the pyramid and near the disc, two wide stone bowls of smoldering copal resin with warm amber embers and thin curls of pale smoke; a few black obsidian shards and jade beads on the slabs. Along the very top and bottom edges, giant dark forest leaves and roots crowd in over the edge as a thin strip. The plaza is cold: near-black shadows, jade-green light; the only warm color is the amber glow of the copal embers. No characters, no animals, no bodies, no cards, no grid.

No text, no letters, no numbers, no glyphs, no hieroglyphs, no real-world scripts, no carvings that look like writing or numerals, no occult symbols, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no border or frame around the picture. No gore, no blood, no skulls, no sacrifice, no horror grotesque.

Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Light tells the story: a few strong sources — veins of crystal in the earth, pale roots and fallen leaves that glow from within — throw cold white-green light upward, the light comes from below. Cold and warm light contrast. Glowing spores, pollen and tiny motes float in the light. Moderate detail, clean readable forms. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime, no cartoon.

Enemy card portrait, 4:5, shown small on the battle field (about 74 px wide) and large in the bestiary, so the enemy must read as one bold, simple, well-lit silhouette against a darker background. Camera at chest height, waist-up: the bottom edge of the picture cuts the body at the waist — head, torso and arms in frame, no hips, no legs; the legs are never visible, whatever the pose. A beast is framed the same way: its head, chest and front legs fill the frame and the bottom edge cuts it behind the shoulders. The figure is centered and fills most of the frame; the head sits in the upper third with a little space above it. The body is turned in a three-quarter view toward the LEFT side of the picture, where its enemies stand; its weapon, its spell or the thing it is named after is thrust toward the left and clearly shown in front of the body. It is an enemy: dangerous, alive and caught in action — not a model posing, not a statue. Its story reads from its body, its pose and the place around it. No one in this set wears a hood unless its own description says so. World: the Underground Forest, the finished creation of the god Vial deep under the city of Endalor — what his Workshop of Forms left half-done is finished here. A forest without a sun: giant trees with pale, almost white trunks drink white-green light from glowing veins of crystal deep in the earth; their leaves glow cold white-green, the air is thick with drifting glowing spores, and a dark cave vault is lost high above the canopy. Its hunters are finished elves: tall and lean, long pointed ears, fine narrow faces, both hands, clothes of woven bast and bark strips; their skin is pale as the trunks, smooth and matte like fine dense clay — they are the god's finished work, not living people, calm and unhurried. Its beasts are bigger than the beasts of the surface and move in packs. Colors: muted and cold, like all our enemies — bone-white bark, pale grey-green moss, dark bottle green, ash grey, a little honey-tan bast and dull ochre; everything else sinks into near-black shadow. Light, the same for the whole set: the light comes from below — cold white-green light glowing from within veins of crystal in the earth, pale roots and fallen leaves rises onto the figure and lights it from underneath; crisp cold white-green rim light on its edges; the only warm colors are the honey-tan of bast and a dull ochre. Background: its own place in the Underground Forest, darker and softer than the figure, with depth. All fourteen portraits of this set share the same framing, painting style, palette and lighting.

The enemy: the Echo of Vial, the rune guardian at the road down — the trace of the god himself: a whirlwind of spores, leaves and glowing pollen that keeps its shape only while it moves. It is not a body of flesh: a tall spinning vortex of pale leaves, glowing white-green spores and pale pollen fills the frame from the bottom edge to the top. In the heart of the vortex, for a moment, the upper half of a figure shows through, made of the same leaves and light: a wanderer in a long robe with a deep hood — the hood hides the face in shadow, with only a faint white-green glow where the eyes would be. The figure is turned toward the left and draws a long bow, aiming to the left, and the arrow on the string is a streak of pure wind (Air). The figure is only half there, its edges dissolving into the whirling leaves. Background: the dark Underground Forest bending under its wind — pale trunks leaning, leaves torn from the branches and drawn into the vortex, white-green light from the ground below.

No text, no letters, no numbers, no glyphs, no runes, no real-world scripts, no carvings that look like writing or numerals, no occult symbols, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no border or frame around the picture. No gore, no blood, no wounds, no skulls, no horror grotesque. No purple, no violet, no magenta light.

items.model_text:
While the artwork beautifully captures the 'Priest of the Knotted Cord' and the desired 'Hatun-Rumi' aesthetic, the inclusion of the dwarf's feet contradicts the instruction for a waist-up portrait where 'no legs, no boots, no feet' are visible. Additionally, the glowing ground lacks the explicit texture of quartz veins. I am regenerating the image to ensure the composition cuts at the waist and to refine the lighting to strictly emanate from the ground fissures.

To better align with this vision for an elite mage of Hatun-Rumi, I will adjust the composition to fully commit to the specified waist-up framing while retaining the character's intricate details and the environmental context. I will shift the lower border upwards to the character’s waist, cutting the portrait at the belt to ensure the body, beard, and headdress remain the central focus without including the hips or legs. The action must be preserved by keeping the bundle of cords and the vibrant green time loop to the left in prominent view. In the background, I will use a high-altitude night setting featuring fitted stone architecture, cliffs, and snowy peaks to add narrative depth. Finally, I will strictly adhere to the lighting principles by generating all glow from the cracks in the granite and quartz veins, effectively illuminating the scene while maintaining deep, near-black shadows.

items.model_text:
Here is a list of stylistic revisions to ensure the model captures the correct 'alive and in action' feel of the creature:

1.  **Anatomy Placement**: The prompt requested one head with three faces on the *bull's* head. The current result depicts human faces perched on the *bull's neck*, with a separate bull head below. I have adjusted this so that the three-faced bearded man’s head replaces the animal bull head entirely.
2.  **Texture Shift**: To move away from the look of a statue, I have replaced the uniform, metallic brass-like texture with organic materials. The main hide is now dark brown fur, contrasted with specific patches of textured grey stone skin on the shoulders and back.
3.  **Color Saturation**: I have muted the palette by replacing the vibrant lavender tones with the specified cold, deep lapis blue and natural, dusty grey masonry.
4.  **Lighting Origin**: I have focused the cold violet light to emanate exclusively from the *cracks* within the alabaster floor and wall inlays, rather than casting a generalized background haze.

items.prompt:

Enemy card portrait, 4:5, shown small on the battle field (about 74 px wide) and large in the bestiary. Camera at chest height, waist-up: the bottom edge of the picture cuts the body at the waist — head, torso and arms in frame, no hips, no legs; the legs are never visible, whatever the pose. The figure is centered and fills most of the frame; the head sits in the upper third with a little space above it. The body is turned in a three-quarter view toward the LEFT side of the picture, where its enemies stand; its weapon, its spell or the thing it is named after is thrust toward the left and clearly shown in front of the body. It is an enemy: dangerous, alive and caught in action — not a model posing, not a statue. Its story reads from its body, its pose and the place around it. Dwarves are short, but the camera is just as close: the bottom edge of the picture cuts the dwarf at the belt — no legs, no boots, no feet in the picture. World: these are the people of Hatun-Rumi, an ancient mountain civilization of dwarves: terraces cut into steep mountainsides, walls of huge many-sided stones fitted together without mortar so tightly that no blade fits between them, roads carved along the cliffs, swaying rope bridges of braided grass over deep gorges; instead of writing they kept long cords with knots; their lords carried the roads down into the valleys and bound every valley to their terraces. items.title: Память: осколок древней редкости (5 из 7)
items.source: Слова автора 29.09.2026 — осколки условного зеркала; ADR-0027 — древняя: красная; GDD §2.4–§2.6
items.prompt:
Dark fantasy game art with a menacing, gloomy, mystical atmosphere. Digital painting with soft transitions, elaborate shadows and an artistic emphasis on details. Lighting effects bring it to life: magical glow, aura and embers, light that comes from inside the subject and from below. Rich worn materials: dark forged iron, old gold, weathered stone, carst crystals glowing from within. Precious, dramatic, high contrast.

Format: game UI icon of a Memory of the Wanderer, square, no border around the picture. One shard of a broken magic mirror, upright, centered, floating in the dark, about 80% of the canvas high. The shard floats on pitch black: everything around it is solid pure black to the very edges of the canvas, never white or grey. All eight icons of this set are one series with one and the same shard: the same silhouette, size and angle; only the light inside tells them apart. The silhouette: a broad jagged piece of mirror glass, about two thirds as wide as it is tall — one long sharp point at the top, a long almost straight left edge, a right edge broken into two straight segments with a small notch between them, and a jagged bottom edge that rises from the lower left corner to the lower right; straight fracture lines and sharp corners, never rounded, never drop- or almond-shaped. It is mirror glass, not a gemstone: a flat pane of thick polished glass seen straight on, its face smooth and glossy with no cut facets like a jewel; the broken edges are thick bevelled glass that catches crisp bright light, and behind the glass a thin layer of old tarnished silver — the backing of the mirror — shows along the whole broken contour as a bright silver rim. Fine hairline cracks run in from the broken edges. Deep inside the glass, as if far behind its surface, lives a reflection that is a memory: blurred light and soft haze, like something remembered through mist. No faces, no figures, no eyes, no text, no runes or symbols in it. The glass is never pitch black inside: even its darkest depths keep a visible tone. A bare shard: no frame, no setting, no metal caps, no stand, no base; no other shards, splinters, sparks or particles floating around it. All the detail lives inside the silhouette. It must stay readable at a tiny size, 24 px: one bold solid shape with a clear bright outline.

Memory: Ancient, the fifth of seven. Deep red (#E85A4E): far behind the glass a whirl of crimson flame swirls around the center and lights the shard from within; the hairline cracks glow red.

The background is solid pure black (#000000), flat, edge to edge: no gradient, no texture, no floor, no cast shadow, no vignette, no checkerboard. Any glow stays close to the subject and fades into the black within a short distance. The whole icon with its glow fits inside the central 80% of the canvas in both width and height: an empty black margin of at least a tenth of the canvas stays on every side — top, bottom, left and right.

No text, no letters, no numbers, no real-world alphabets, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements.

items.title: Негнущаяся кукла — Библиотека Улариона, рядовой 1, физ ДД силы, дворфы, Земля (глубокий промт)
items.source: docs/content/враги-биомов.md, раздел 3, рядовые, № 1: «Каменный дворф без шарниров в локтях и коленях; ходит прямо и бьёт всем телом»; способность b3o1 «Каменный осколок» — Земля.dmg.grp, удар по группе: осколки веером. Прежний вариант — art/generated/enemies/b3-o1-unbending-puppet__nb2.jpg: манекен в рост с вытянутыми руками и пустыми глазами
items.prompt:
Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Epic, dramatic character art: a powerful pose, a low camera, strong theatrical light from below. Light tells the story: a few strong sources — the sand of hourglasses, cracks in the stone floor and fine grooves in old stone that glow from within — throw warm amber light upward, the light comes from below. Warm and cold light contrast. Dust motes and fine stone grit float in the light. Moderate detail, clean readable forms; the face, the hands and the weapon get the most detail. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime, no cartoon.

Draw exactly one image in a single pass: no alternative versions, no second attempts, no text in the reply. Enemy card portrait, 4:5. The card is shown small on the battle field (about 74 px wide) and large in the bestiary, so the enemy must read as one bold, simple, well-lit silhouette with a clear pose against a darker background. Framing: a close, heroic half-length portrait. The camera is a little below the figure's chest and looks slightly up, so the enemy towers over the viewer and fills most of the frame. A figure shaped like a dwarf is cut by the bottom edge of the picture at the belt: head, shoulders, chest, arms and hands in the frame, no hips, no legs, no feet. Beasts and machines are framed as their own description says. The head sits in the upper third with a little space above it. The body is turned in three-quarter view toward the LEFT side of the picture, where its enemies stand; its weapon, its spell or the thing it is named after is thrust toward the left, in front of the body, and reads clearly. Pathos: it is a worthy and dangerous enemy — powerful, proud, alive and caught at the peak of an action, a foe that is frightening and honourable to defeat. Its character shows in its face, its gaze and its posture; its story shows in the details of its body and its tools. No one in this set wears a hood. World: the Library of Ularion, the workshop of the god of knowledge deep under the city of Endalor — a real ancient library cut in dark stone. Its halls go down and down; on long stone shelves lie stone tablets and stone cylinders covered with fine engraved grooves — the writing that only the god can read; it shows only as a worn texture of fine lines, never as letters or signs. On the worktables parts of dwarves and parts of mechanisms lie together: the god made the people and the machine with the same hands. At every work place stands an hourglass of bronze and glass with glowing amber sand. Stone beetles live in the shelves; stone sagans are rock that has noticed itself. The Library's servants are stone dwarves made by the god. The Library calls them puppets, but they are masterworks, made carefully and with pride: carved from dark grey stone with the precision of great sculpture, polished smooth where they move and left with fine chisel marks elsewhere; the proportions of dwarf warriors — very broad shoulders, a deep chest, a thick neck, massive forearms, big capable hands; strong individual faces with heavy brows and broad noses, carved beards bound with bronze rings; bronze ball joints at the neck, shoulders, elbows and wrists — precise, well-oiled work with thin engraved bands of straight lines. Their eyes are inlaid stones that glow from within, amber unless the description says otherwise: alive, attentive, fixed on the enemy with purpose. Their hands know the work and the fight; only the writing they cannot understand. They move with weight and certainty, like veteran warriors and master craftsmen. Colors: muted, like all our enemies — dark grey basalt, warm dull bronze and old brass, soot black, dusty ochre; everything else sinks into near-black shadow. Light, the same for the whole set: the light comes from below — warm amber light from the sand of the hourglasses, from cracks in the stone floor and from the grooves of the tablets rises onto the figure and lights its face and hands from underneath; crisp cool grey-blue rim light on its edges is the only cold light. Background: its own place in the Library, darker and softer than the figure, with depth. All fourteen portraits of this set share the same framing, painting style, palette and lighting.

The enemy: the Unbending, a rank-and-file brawler of the Library (Earth). Who he is: a stone dwarf warrior whom the god carved without joints at the elbows — each arm is a single piece of dark stone from the bronze ball of the shoulder to the heavy square fist. He was made to hold the line and never bend, and right now he wants one thing: to break through the heroes on the left. Character: unyielding, stubborn, proud that he has never bowed. It shows in his face: a heavy brow lowered, a jaw clenched like a vice, nostrils flared, amber eyes burning steadily at his foe; his neck and back are straight as a pillar. Pose, the moment of the blow: he cannot bend, so he strikes with his whole body. His weight is thrown forward toward the left and his torso is twisted hard from the waist in a huge horizontal sweep: the near arm, straight and rigid like a stone club, swings across the front of his body toward the left, fist first, and has just smashed into stone — a wide fan of sharp stone shards bursts toward the left from the point of impact (Earth); the far arm, just as straight, is flung back behind him by the force of the swing. His chin is tucked and his head lowered behind his leading shoulder like a ram's, eyes fixed on the target. Details that tell his story: (1) where the elbows should be, the stone runs on unbroken, and a plain bronze band is sealed around it — he was made this way on purpose; (2) his square fists are chipped and worn smooth by a thousand blows; (3) his beard is carved straight and stiff like a spade, without braids, bound by one heavy bronze ring; (4) a heavy bronze collar sits on his shoulders like a yoke; (5) a web of old cracks across his chest has been filled with bronze by the Library's fitters. Place: a long straight aisle between tall stone shelves; behind him a thick stone pillar bears a fist-shaped crater with cracks running out of it; amber light glows from the cracks of the floor below.

No text, no letters, no numbers, no glyphs, no runes that look like letters, no real-world scripts, no carvings that look like writing or numerals, no occult symbols, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no border or frame around the picture. Tablets, cylinders, cords and walls carry no writing and no signs: only fine worn grooves and texture. No gore, no blood, no skulls, no horror grotesque. No purple, no violet, no magenta light. Only one figure in the foreground; a figure shaped like a dwarf has exactly two arms and two hands. Not a mannequin, not a crash-test dummy, not a marionette on strings, not a clumsy golem, not a robot, not a statue on display: no stiff, passive, awkward or doll-like pose, no dead or empty eyes.

items.source: docs/content/враги-биомов.md, раздел 3, рядовые, № 1: «Каменный дворф без шарниров в локтях и коленях; ходит прямо и бьёт всем телом»; способность b3o1 «Каменный осколок» — Земля.dmg.grp, удар по группе: осколки веером. Прежний вариант — art/generated/enemies/b3-o1-unbending-puppet__nb2.jpg: манекен в рост с вытянутыми руками и пустыми глазами. v2: в v1 лицо и мощь верные, но ближняя рука согнута в бронзовом локте — рамка кадра давала шарниры в локтях всем; рамка теперь «если описание не говорит иначе», рука — прямая балка
items.prompt:
Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Epic, dramatic character art: a powerful pose, a low camera, strong theatrical light from below. Light tells the story: a few strong sources — the sand of hourglasses, cracks in the stone floor and fine grooves in old stone that glow from within — throw warm amber light upward, the light comes from below. Warm and cold light contrast. Dust motes and fine stone grit float in the light. Moderate detail, clean readable forms; the face, the hands and the weapon get the most detail. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime, no cartoon.

Draw exactly one image in a single pass: no alternative versions, no second attempts, no text in the reply. Enemy card portrait, 4:5. The card is shown small on the battle field (about 74 px wide) and large in the bestiary, so the enemy must read as one bold, simple, well-lit silhouette with a clear pose against a darker background. Framing: a close, heroic half-length portrait. The camera is a little below the figure's chest and looks slightly up, so the enemy towers over the viewer and fills most of the frame. A figure shaped like a dwarf is cut by the bottom edge of the picture at the belt: head, shoulders, chest, arms and hands in the frame, no hips, no legs, no feet. Beasts and machines are framed as their own description says. The head sits in the upper third with a little space above it. The body is turned in three-quarter view toward the LEFT side of the picture, where its enemies stand; its weapon, its spell or the thing it is named after is thrust toward the left, in front of the body, and reads clearly. Pathos: it is a worthy and dangerous enemy — powerful, proud, alive and caught at the peak of an action, a foe that is frightening and honourable to defeat. Its character shows in its face, its gaze and its posture; its story shows in the details of its body and its tools. No one in this set wears a hood. World: the Library of Ularion, the workshop of the god of knowledge deep under the city of Endalor — a real ancient library cut in dark stone. Its halls go down and down; on long stone shelves lie stone tablets and stone cylinders covered with fine engraved grooves — the writing that only the god can read; it shows only as a worn texture of fine lines, never as letters or signs. On the worktables parts of dwarves and parts of mechanisms lie together: the god made the people and the machine with the same hands. At every work place stands an hourglass of bronze and glass with glowing amber sand. Stone beetles live in the shelves; stone sagans are rock that has noticed itself. The Library's servants are stone dwarves made by the god. The Library calls them puppets, but they are masterworks, made carefully and with pride: carved from dark grey stone with the precision of great sculpture, polished smooth where they move and left with fine chisel marks elsewhere; the proportions of dwarf warriors — very broad shoulders, a deep chest, a thick neck, massive forearms, big capable hands; strong individual faces with heavy brows and broad noses, carved beards bound with bronze rings; bronze ball joints — precise, well-oiled work with thin engraved bands of straight lines — at the neck, shoulders, elbows and wrists, unless the description says otherwise. Their eyes are inlaid stones that glow from within, amber unless the description says otherwise: alive, attentive, fixed on the enemy with purpose. Their hands know the work and the fight; only the writing they cannot understand. They move with weight and certainty, like veteran warriors and master craftsmen. Colors: muted, like all our enemies — dark grey basalt, warm dull bronze and old brass, soot black, dusty ochre; everything else sinks into near-black shadow. Light, the same for the whole set: the light comes from below — warm amber light from the sand of the hourglasses, from cracks in the stone floor and from the grooves of the tablets rises onto the figure and lights its face and hands from underneath; crisp cool grey-blue rim light on its edges is the only cold light. Background: its own place in the Library, darker and softer than the figure, with depth. All fourteen portraits of this set share the same framing, painting style, palette and lighting.

The enemy: the Unbending, a rank-and-file brawler of the Library (Earth). Who he is: a stone dwarf warrior whom the god carved without elbows — each arm is a single straight piece of dark stone from the bronze ball of the shoulder to the heavy square fist, with no joint and no bend anywhere along it. He was made to hold the line and never bend, and right now he wants one thing: to break through the heroes on the left. Character: unyielding, stubborn, proud that he has never bowed. It shows in his face: a heavy brow lowered, a jaw clenched like a vice, nostrils flared, amber eyes burning steadily at his foe; his neck and back are straight as a pillar. Pose, the moment of the blow: he cannot bend his arms, so he strikes with his whole body. His weight is thrown forward toward the left and his torso is twisted hard toward the left. His near arm is a straight, rigid stone beam from shoulder to fist; it is swung out straight toward the left at shoulder height like a battering beam, and its fist has just smashed into stone near the left edge of the picture — a wide fan of sharp stone shards bursts toward the left from the point of impact (Earth). His far arm, just as straight and rigid, is flung up and back behind him by the force of the swing. His chin is tucked and his head lowered behind his leading shoulder like a ram's, eyes fixed on the target. Details that tell his story: (1) where the elbows should be, the stone runs on unbroken, and a plain bronze band is sealed around it — he was made this way on purpose; (2) his square fists are chipped and worn smooth by a thousand blows; (3) his beard is carved straight and stiff like a spade, without braids, bound by one heavy bronze ring; (4) a heavy bronze collar sits on his shoulders like a yoke; (5) a web of old cracks across his chest has been filled with bronze by the Library's fitters. Place: a long straight aisle between tall stone shelves; behind him a thick stone pillar bears a fist-shaped crater with cracks running out of it; amber light glows from the cracks of the floor below.

No text, no letters, no numbers, no glyphs, no runes that look like letters, no real-world scripts, no carvings that look like writing or numerals, no occult symbols, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no border or frame around the picture. Tablets, cylinders, cords and walls carry no writing and no signs: only fine worn grooves and texture. No gore, no blood, no skulls, no horror grotesque. No purple, no violet, no magenta light. Only one figure in the foreground; a figure shaped like a dwarf has exactly two arms and two hands. Not a mannequin, not a crash-test dummy, not a marionette on strings, not a clumsy golem, not a robot, not a statue on display: no stiff, passive, awkward or doll-like pose, no dead or empty eyes.

items.prompt:
Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Epic, dramatic character art: a powerful pose, a low camera, strong theatrical light from below. Light tells the story: a few strong sources — the sand of hourglasses, cracks in the stone floor and fine grooves in old stone that glow from within — throw warm amber light upward, the light comes from below. Warm and cold light contrast. Dust motes and fine stone grit float in the light. Moderate detail, clean readable forms; the face, the hands and the weapon get the most detail. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime, no cartoon.

Draw exactly one image in a single pass: no alternative versions, no second attempts, no text in the reply. Enemy card portrait, 4:5. The card is shown small on the battle field (about 74 px wide) and large in the bestiary, so the enemy must read as one bold, simple, well-lit silhouette with a clear pose against a darker background. Framing: a close, heroic half-length portrait. The camera is a little below the figure's chest and looks slightly up, so the enemy towers over the viewer and fills most of the frame. A figure shaped like a dwarf is cut by the bottom edge of the picture at the belt: head, shoulders, chest, arms and hands in the frame, no hips, no legs, no feet. Beasts and machines are framed as their own description says. The head sits in the upper third with a little space above it. The body is turned in three-quarter view toward the LEFT side of the picture, where its enemies stand; its weapon, its spell or the thing it is named after is thrust toward the left, in front of the body, and reads clearly. Pathos: it is a worthy and dangerous enemy — powerful, proud, alive and caught at the peak of an action, a foe that is frightening and honourable to defeat. Its character shows in its face, its gaze and its posture; its story shows in the details of its body and its tools. No one in this set wears a hood. World: the Library of Ularion, the workshop of the god of knowledge deep under the city of Endalor — a real ancient library cut in dark stone. Its halls go down and down; on long stone shelves lie stone tablets and stone cylinders covered with long, straight, parallel engraved grooves, like ruled lines with nothing written between them — the writing that only the god can read shows only as this worn texture of straight lines, never as letters, squiggles or signs. On the worktables parts of dwarves and parts of mechanisms lie together: the god made the people and the machine with the same hands. At every work place stands an hourglass of bronze and glass with glowing amber sand. Stone beetles live in the shelves; stone sagans are rock that has noticed itself. The Library's servants are stone dwarves made by the god. The Library calls them puppets, but they are masterworks, made carefully and with pride: carved from dark grey stone with the precision of great sculpture, polished smooth where they move and left with fine chisel marks elsewhere; the proportions of dwarf warriors — very broad shoulders, a deep chest, a thick neck, massive forearms, big capable hands; strong individual faces with heavy brows and broad noses, carved beards bound with bronze rings; bronze ball joints — precise, well-oiled work with thin engraved bands of straight lines — at the neck, shoulders, elbows and wrists, unless the description says otherwise. Their eyes are inlaid stones that glow from within, amber unless the description says otherwise: alive, attentive, fixed on the enemy with purpose. Their hands know the work and the fight; only the writing they cannot understand. They move with weight and certainty, like veteran warriors and master craftsmen. Colors: muted, like all our enemies — dark grey basalt, warm dull bronze and old brass, soot black, dusty ochre; everything else sinks into near-black shadow. Light, the same for the whole set: the light comes from below — warm amber light from the sand of the hourglasses, from cracks in the stone floor and from the grooves of the tablets rises onto the figure and lights its face and hands from underneath; crisp cool grey-blue rim light on its edges is the only cold light. Background: its own place in the Library, darker and softer than the figure, with depth. All fourteen portraits of this set share the same framing, painting style, palette and lighting.

EDIT MODE — this overrides everything above: do not draw a new picture, edit the attached image. The attached image is the current portrait of this enemy, the Unbending: a grey stone dwarf with a bronze collar who smashes his straight stone arm into a pillar at the left, stone shards flying. Keep the picture exactly as it is — the same figure, face, beard, collar, cracks, the straight arm with the bronze band, the fist, the shards, the pillar with the fist-shaped crater, the shelves, the hourglasses, the light, the colors and the painting style. Change only the raised arm at the top right of the picture: now it bends in the middle at a bronze ball. Make it one straight, rigid stone beam from the shoulder to the fist, with no joint and no bend anywhere along it: it rises straight up and a little back from his shoulder, and its fist is at the top, near the top edge. Remove the bronze ball in the middle of that arm; a plain bronze band around the middle of the arm, like the one on the other arm, is fine. Nothing else changes.

No text, no letters, no numbers, no glyphs, no runes that look like letters, no real-world scripts, no carvings that look like writing or numerals, no occult symbols, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no border or frame around the picture. Tablets, cylinders, cords and walls carry no writing and no signs: only fine worn grooves and texture. No gore, no blood, no skulls, no horror grotesque. No purple, no violet, no magenta light. Only one figure in the foreground; a figure shaped like a dwarf has exactly two arms and two hands. Not a mannequin, not a crash-test dummy, not a marionette on strings, not a clumsy golem, not a robot, not a statue on display: no stiff, passive, awkward or doll-like pose, no dead or empty eyes.

Light tells the story: a few strong sources — the sand of hourglasses, cracks in the stone floor and fine grooves in old stone that glow from within — throw warm amber light upward, the light comes from below. Warm and cold light contrast. Dust motes and fine stone grit float in the light. Moderate detail, clean readable forms; the face, the hands and the weapon get the most detail. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime, no cartoon.

Draw exactly one image in a single pass: no alternative versions, no second attempts, no text in the reply. Enemy card portrait, 4:5. The card is shown small on the battle field (about 74 px wide) and large in the bestiary, so the enemy must read as one bold, simple, well-lit silhouette with a clear pose against a darker background. Framing: a close, heroic half-length portrait. The camera is a little below the figure's chest and looks slightly up, so the enemy towers over the viewer and fills most of the frame. A figure shaped like a dwarf is cut by the bottom edge of the picture at the belt: head, shoulders, chest, arms and hands in the frame, no hips, no legs, no feet. Beasts and machines are framed as their own description says. The head sits in the upper third with a little space above it. The body is turned in three-quarter view toward the LEFT side of the picture, where its enemies stand; its weapon, its spell or the thing it is named after is thrust toward the left, in front of the body, and reads clearly. Pathos: it is a worthy and dangerous enemy — powerful, proud, alive and caught at the peak of an action, a foe that is frightening and honourable to defeat. Its character shows in its face, its gaze and its posture; its story shows in the details of its body and its tools. No one in this set wears a hood. World: the Library of Ularion, the workshop of the god of knowledge deep under the city of Endalor — a real ancient library cut in dark stone. Its halls go down and down; on long stone shelves lie stone tablets and stone cylinders covered with long, straight, parallel engraved grooves, like ruled lines with nothing written between them — the writing that only the god can read shows only as this worn texture of straight lines, never as letters, squiggles or signs. On the worktables parts of dwarves and parts of mechanisms lie together: the god made the people and the machine with the same hands. At every work place stands an hourglass of bronze and glass with glowing amber sand. Stone beetles live in the shelves; stone sagans are rock that has noticed itself. The Library's servants are stone dwarves made by the god. The Library calls them puppets, but they are masterworks, made carefully and with pride: carved from dark grey stone with the precision of great sculpture, polished smooth where they move and left with fine chisel marks elsewhere; the proportions of dwarf warriors — very broad shoulders, a deep chest, a thick neck, massive forearms, big capable hands; strong individual faces with heavy brows and broad noses, carved beards bound with bronze rings; bronze ball joints — precise, well-oiled work with thin engraved bands of straight lines — at the neck, shoulders, elbows and wrists, unless the description says otherwise. Their eyes are inlaid stones that glow from within, amber unless the description says otherwise: alive, attentive, fixed on the enemy with purpose. Their hands know the work and the fight; only the writing they cannot understand. They move with weight and certainty, like veteran warriors and master craftsmen. Turn it into an open stone slab — two thick, flat leaves of dark stone joined by bronze hinges and opened like a book, their inner faces smooth stone blazing with amber light: no paper pages, no page edges, no marks. His hand holds it in the same place. Nothing else changes.

Subject: Astrid Half-Grosh, a woman of the northern lands, a warrior of great strength of the Fire school. Who she is: of the northern women, only three in a generation go to the arena sands and on campaigns, and the north knew her by her second blade — a fire stone was set into it when she was twenty. On the campaign against the southern elven forest the jarl gave her the purse of the campaign: the second halves of split coins for the hired strangers, who had taken the first halves in advance. Pose, the moment of the charge: she charges toward the right, her weight thrown onto her leading shoulder, her torso twisting into the swing. Her near hand holds a broad northern sword low and back, ready to sweep up; her far hand raises the second blade high above her shoulder — a shorter, heavy blade with a scarlet fire stone set at the base of the blade, glowing like a coal, flames licking along its edge (Fire). Her head is lowered, chin tucked, eyes fixed on the enemy beyond the right edge. Subject: Eavin the Carver, an elven woman of the southern forest, a swift archer of the Air school. Who she is: a master bowyer who carved bows out of living trees without felling them: she took only as much as the trunk would give, and the tree grew on. That was her key. She had many pupils, but every one of them cut across the grain at least once, so for two hundred years she argued with the elders that a secret is better carried away than left half-kept. Her last bow she carved from the tree under which she asked to be laid. Character: proud, uncompromising and exacting — a master who accepts nothing by halves. Her face: ageless, looking about fifty by human measure, fine lines at the eyes, high sharp cheekbones, long pointed elven ears, a narrow proud mouth; silver-streaked dark hair tied back tightly with a strip of bark; grey-green eyes narrowed along the arrow, cool and certain. Pose, the moment of the shot: she has turned sharply toward the right in one fluid movement and loosed an arrow: her bow arm is fully extended toward the right, the bow canted, the string still quivering; her drawing hand has just released beside her jaw and is opening, fingers spread; her shoulders are square to the shot, her chin raised. A spiral of white-green wind (Air) follows the arrow toward the right edge, tearing leaves and fine wood shavings along with it. Details that tell her story: (1) her bow is living wood: bark still on its back, fine growth rings on its face, and a few young green leaves sprouting from its tips; (2) a crooked carving knife with a worn antler handle hangs at her belt, and curls of pale wood shavings are caught in her sleeves; (3) her fingers are a carver's — callused, with thin white scars, a leather thumb guard on the drawing hand; (4) a sash of woven bast across her chest holds a few arrows fletched with grey feathers; (5) behind her the trunk of a colossal living tree bears a fresh, smooth notch cut exactly to the width of a palm. Pale white-green light of the Air school rises from the mossy roots below and from small crystals among them; leaves and shavings drift in the wind.

Subject: Elias, a homeless archer of the roads, a human man, a swift archer of the Air school. Who he is: he guarded caravans for food and never asked where they went. On a southern road he carried a fallen elven wanderer into the shade, and she gave him a scroll that would admit him to the great Tree of the elves. He did not go to the Tree — he went after her. With her small band he walked the old roads, and for the first time he had a home, only it was always on the move. He learned to shoot so quietly that he never woke the sleepers in camp. His face: in his thirties, lean and weathered, a short dark beard, dark hair tied back, a thin scar through one eyebrow, calm dark eyes utterly focused; his lips pressed together, holding his breath. Pose, the moment before the shot: he stands between the sleeping camp and the dark, his body turned toward the right, and draws a long plain bow to full draw toward the right; the fletching touches the corner of his mouth, the drawing elbow is high behind him, the bow arm straight and steady; his head is tilted slightly to the arrow, eyes on the enemy beyond the right edge. Subject: Oelis the Unlayering, a woman of a forgotten people who lived long before all the cities that stand today, a controller and battle mage of the Time school. Who she is: her people were as many as the stars over the river, and every craft had its own key — not a word, but the way you hold your hand. Her key was to take the years off things, layer by layer, the way bark is peeled, until the new showed through under the old: a cracked wall came out of her hands whole, a black bowl came out bright as on the day it was fired. Their city stood by the water and was built of white clay. This hero is one of the Faceless: a soul of the distant past whose face has long been worn away, and who does not remember who they were. items.prompt:
Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Epic, heroic character art: a powerful pose, a low camera, strong light from below. Light tells the story: a few strong sources — crystals and cracks that glow from within — throw colored light upward, the light comes from below. Cold and warm light contrast. Dust motes and grains of sand float in the light. Moderate detail, clean readable forms; the face, the hands and the weapon get the most detail. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime. Match the brushwork, lighting and color handling of the attached style reference images, but do NOT copy their subjects, objects, letters or composition.

Draw exactly one image in a single pass: no alternative versions, no second attempts, no text in the reply. Format: vertical hero card portrait, 4:5. A close, heroic half-body portrait from the waist or hips up, three-quarter view; no knees, no legs, no feet in the frame. The camera is a little below the hero's chest and looks slightly up, so the hero towers — a legend, not an extra. The hero's body is turned toward the right side of the picture, toward unseen enemies beyond the right edge, and the face is seen in three-quarter view looking to the right. The hero is caught at the peak of an action that shows who they are; the pose carries weight and intent. Head in the upper third, the face large, well lit and readable at small size, with a clear expression; the lower quarter may be darker because the card puts the name there. Rich atmospheric background that tells where the hero lived, with depth and soft focus, darker than the character. Light comes from below and from glowing crystals; rim light separates the figure from the background.

The hero belongs to the people of the white hills — a forgotten people who lived long before all the peoples of today, on the rolling hills of white chalk at the edge of the great dark forest of Ish-Kantun. They look unlike any people living now: tall and lean, with long necks, long narrow faces, high cheekbones and large deep-set eyes; their skin has the warm grey-brown tone of river clay, and they paint lines and handprints of white chalk from their hills on their faces and arms. They wear undyed woven cloth and wraps of pale bark-cloth, necklaces of white shells and chalk beads; their tools are old and simple — wood, bone, white flint, woven vine, fired clay. Their enemies were the long-lived forest elves of Ish-Kantun with feathered cloaks, jade masks and black obsidian blades, who came out of the forest when their Great Count ended; such things appear only as trophies or as the threat beyond the right edge.

Subject: Aitan Net-of-Vines, a man of the white hills, a trapper who binds enemies, of the Earth school. Who he is: on the forest paths where the feathered archers of Ish-Kantun came down toward the hills, he strung nets of living lianas between the trees, and whole files of archers never reached the hills. Right now an archer has stepped onto his path, and he throws. Character: patient, silent and cunning, a hunter who waits for hours and strikes once. His brows are drawn low, his eyes narrowed and fixed on the prey beyond the right edge, his mouth a thin calm line — no hurry in him at all. Pose, the moment of the throw: the camera is low; he has just hurled a great net of woven green lianas toward the right: it unfurls wide in the air in front of him, its weighted edges of white flint spreading out; his near arm follows through the throw, extended toward the right, the hand still open; his far hand grips the long trailing rope of the net close to his chest, ready to pull it shut. His shoulders twist into the throw, his long body leans forward. Amber-orange light of the Earth school rises from the ground, and small stones and clods jump up around the roots as the net's rope tightens. Решение агента: миг заклинания — кричит имя, кольцо зелёного света Времени держит фигуру из фиолетового тумана; тростниковое стило за ухом и в руке, закрытая писчая дощечка у пояса (без знаков). К выгрузке — art/generated/heroes/hero-c2-53-kersu__nb2.jpg → design/ui/assets/art/heroes/c2-53.jpg. v2: v1 плоская, светлая, почти без теней — теперь ночь, факелы, ветер

Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Epic, heroic character art: a powerful pose, a low camera, strong light from below. Light tells the story: a few strong sources — crystals and cracks that glow from within — throw colored light upward, the light comes from below. Cold and warm light contrast. Dust motes and grains of sand float in the light. Moderate detail, clean readable forms; the face, the hands and the weapon get the most detail. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime. Match the brushwork, lighting and color handling of the attached style reference images, but do NOT copy their subjects, objects, letters or composition.

Draw exactly one image in a single pass: no alternative versions, no second attempts, no text in the reply. Format: vertical hero card portrait, 4:5. A close, heroic half-body portrait from the waist or hips up, three-quarter view: the bottom edge of the picture cuts the body at the belt or the hips; no knees, no legs, no feet in the frame, whatever the pose. The camera is a little below the hero's chest and looks slightly up, so the hero towers — a legend, not an extra. The hero's body is turned toward the right side of the picture, toward unseen enemies beyond the right edge, and the face is seen in three-quarter view looking to the right. The hero is caught at the peak of an action that shows who they are; the pose carries weight and intent. Head in the upper third, the face large, well lit and readable at small size, with a clear expression. The lower part of the picture sinks gradually into deeper shadow — no band, no plate, nothing written. Rich atmospheric background that tells where the hero lived, with depth and soft focus, darker than the character. Light comes from below and from glowing crystals; rim light separates the figure from the background.

The hero belongs to the people of one face — a forgotten people who lived long before all the peoples of today, in a walled city of sun-dried brick on a green river plain, not far from the gates of Meshen-Gar. A person of this people has one face and one name for life, and at the city gate everyone names themselves aloud. They look unlike any people living now: their faces are bare, calm and strongly drawn — broad brows, straight noses, full lips and very large, steady eyes of clear dark amber; their skin is a warm olive-gold with a smooth matte look, like fine clay; the men keep short trimmed beards, the women wear their dark hair in one plain braid; none of them ever wears a mask or paints the face. They wear long plain robes and wraps of undyed wool and linen with a single coloured band at the hem, wide leather belts and simple bronze; their city has walls of sun-dried brick and gates of heavy cedar beams. Their enemies were the Many-Faced of Meshen-Gar — people who changed their own bodies at will, growing wings, horns, stone skin or a second face; winged bulls with the faces of men guarded their gates, and their priests wore masks over masks; in the Tide of Forms they spread over the land like a flood of violet mist and took the face of everyone they touched; such things appear only as trophies or as the threat beyond the right edge.

Subject: Kersu Form-Holder, a man of the people of one face, a controller of the Time school. Who he is: he sat at the city gate as a scribe and remembered everyone who ever came in — even the traders from Meshen-Gar, who changed their faces the way his people change a belt. When the Tide of Forms began, the Many-Faced came against the city wearing the faces of those they had touched in the fields; he went out to them and called them by the names they had once given at the gate, and for a moment their shape held. Right now a shifting shape comes at him, and he calls out its old name. Character: steadfast, sorrowful and fearless — a quiet keeper of names who hates the familiar faces most, because he remembers how they smiled; his brows drawn, his mouth open in a loud call, his amber eyes wide and fierce. Pose, the moment of the spell: the camera is low; he stands before the gate, turned toward the right, leaning forward into a wind that whips his robe back. He has exactly two arms: his near arm is thrust out toward the right, the finger pointing, and a ring of green light of the Time school shoots from his hand and closes around a shape of shifting violet mist beyond the right edge, holding it still for a moment; his far hand is clenched at his chest around a reed stylus. Details that tell his story: (1) his fingers are stained with dried clay from years at the gate; (2) a second reed stylus is tucked behind his ear; (3) a closed wooden writing board hangs at his hip on a cord; (4) a plain robe with a single blue band at the hem; (5) a grey feather from a changed one's wing is caught on his sleeve. Place: the great cedar gate of his city at night, lit by two torches, walls of sun-dried brick in deep shadow, and beyond them the river plain swallowed by a towering, creeping violet mist. Green light of the Time school rises from the paving stones below; violet mist from the right.

No text, no letters, no numbers, no real-world alphabets, no runes or markings that look like writing, no glyphs, no cuneiform, no wedge-shaped marks, no inscriptions on tablets or walls, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no border or frame around the picture, no name plate, no dark band at the bottom, no gems or badges of rank. No bodies, no skulls, no blood. Only one character in the foreground; a person has exactly two arms and two hands. Not stiff, not passive, not posing like a mannequin; no empty eyes. The hero has exactly one face: no mask worn on the face, no second face, no horns, no wings, no scales or stone skin on the hero.

Light tells the story: it comes from below — from glowing crystals, cracks and gems — cold turquoise (#48E5D4) against warm gold and amber (#DDBC7A, #E6A84B); dust motes and sparks float in the light. Dark fantasy: mystery and gravity, high contrast. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime, no flat vector style.

Draw exactly one image in a single pass: no alternative versions, no second attempts, no text in the reply.

Format: a concept sheet for the hero card of a dark fantasy mobile RPG, landscape 16:9. On a plain dark background — near-black slate (#0C0E11) with a soft vignette, no table, no scenery — stand exactly three vertical hero cards side by side in one row, evenly spaced and the same size. Each card is tall and narrow, in a 9:16 proportion, about five sixths of the canvas high, seen straight on, flat, not tilted, not in perspective, fully inside the canvas with a small margin. The three cards show the same hero in the same card design at three steps of power, from left to right: the left card — a weak hero, fresh and common; the middle card — a strong hero, epic and halfway up; the right card — a legendary hero, timeless and at the very peak. The player must feel the difference in power at a glance, before reading any number: from left to right the frame grows richer, the light brighter, the aura and the particles stronger. Each card may spill its glow and particles onto the dark background around it.

Attached images, in this order: (1) the hero's portrait; (2) the white rarity crystal; (3) the violet rarity crystal; (4) the green rarity crystal; (5) a lit rune stone; (6) an unlit rune stone; (7) the valor icon; (8) the combat power icon; (9) the class icon. They give the exact look of these elements on the cards; do not copy their plain square backgrounds.

The hero, the same on all three cards: the old dwarf from image 1 — a bald head, a stern furrowed face, a long white braided beard, a heavy brown leather coat studded with iron rivets, a round iron-rimmed shield on his arm, a heavy chain with a huge old iron key across his chest. Keep his face, clothes, colors and pose as in image 1. He is painted edge to edge inside the card's window: head in the upper third, shown down to the hips; the dark stone and amber crystals of his portrait fill the window behind him.

Card anatomy — the same on all three cards and in the same places, unless the concept below says otherwise:
- Top center: the rarity crystal from images 2–4, set into the top of the frame: white on the left card, violet on the middle card, green on the right card. One crystal per card.
- Just below the crystal, along the top edge of the window: valor stars in a short arc — small solid four-pointed stars like the star in image 7, without its tile. The number of star places is the hero's personal maximum. Left card: one place, empty — a dark hollow socket. Middle card: three places — two filled with glowing gold, one empty socket. Right card: five places, all five filled and blazing gold.
- Top left corner: a small round badge with the level number: 34 on the left card, 512 on the middle card, 1200 on the right card. Top right corner: the element — a small round medallion of dark iron and old gold with a living piece of glowing amber rock inside (Earth, #EB9D40).
- Five small rune stones like images 5 and 6, set into the frame beside the portrait: three stacked on the left side, two stacked on the right side. Left card: all five unlit, dark grey. Middle card: the three on the left lit with turquoise light inside, the two on the right unlit. Right card: all five lit.
- Bottom: a blank name plaque across the card — smooth, with nothing written on it. Under it one row: the class icon from image 9 (a shield on a hexagonal tile) on the left, and the combat power — the crossed-swords icon from image 8 followed by the number — to its right: 1240 on the left card, 48350 on the middle card, 912780 on the right card.
The digits are clean, bold and legible, in light warm gold.

Concept: Gold Filigree — the frame is a piece of jewellery, and the power shows as the goldsmith's work growing richer. Left card: a plain narrow frame of dull dark bronze with flat edges and no ornament; plain bronze bezels hold the crystal, the star socket and the rune stones; no glow at all, the portrait slightly muted. Middle card: the frame is gilded; delicate gold filigree scrolls curl out of the four corners; a small pointed crest with little gold leaves holds the violet crystal; a soft violet-and-gold glow runs along the inner edge of the window; a few golden sparks drift up from the bottom. Right card: a sumptuous frame of polished old gold with dense openwork filigree along every edge; a tall crest with spread golden wings and rays around a large green crystal; the corners grow into ornate gold flourishes set with small green gems; a warm golden radiance blazes behind the whole card and spills onto the background; embers and bright gold sparks swirl around the card; a short ribbon of plain crimson silk, with nothing written on it, is draped across the top right corner as the sign of the maximum.

No words, no letters, no real-world alphabets, no Roman numerals, no runes, glyphs or markings that look like writing, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no captions, titles or labels above or under the cards. The only characters anywhere in the picture are the digits of the level and combat power numbers given above; the name plaque stays blank. No pentagrams, no occult signs, no crosses; every star is a solid four-pointed star. No phone mockup, no hands holding the cards, no table, no perspective, no tilted or overlapping cards, no fourth card. The hero has exactly two arms and two hands; no empty eyes.
