items.prompt:
Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Epic key art of a legendary place with a sense of great scale and depth. Light tells the story: a few strong sources — crystals, cracks, glowing plants, lava — throw colored light upward, the light comes from below. Cold and warm light contrast. Dust motes, spores, sparks and grains of sand float in the light. Moderate detail, clean readable forms. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime, no cartoon.

Draw exactly one image in a single pass: no alternative versions, no second attempts, no text in the reply. Format: wide cinematic panorama, 21:9 — the full-screen background of the game's Descent window, where the player chooses a place under the city of Endalor and sends a squad of heroes down. The picture shows one place of the Descent and the inhabitants who are waiting for the heroes, as an old storyteller would describe them. The viewer stands at the entrance and looks into the depth; the inhabitants stand in the middle distance and in the depth, turned toward the viewer, calm and dangerous, as if they already know someone is coming. They belong to the scene: full figures at their distance, silhouettes lit from below with a rim of light, the largest and most important ones far away in the depth — never a row of portraits, never a close-up. The game lays its interface over the picture, so the composition leaves room for it: the left quarter of the picture is dark and calm — a near wall, trunks or stacks in deep shadow, no figures and no bright light there; the upper left, from the left quarter to the middle, is a calm dark vault, canopy or haze without figures — the game writes the name of the place there; the bottom fifth falls into shadow — dark floor, no faces there. The path or hall leads into the depth toward a vanishing point at about 60% of the width and 45% of the height; all figures and the brightest light sit in the right two thirds of the picture, between 15% and 80% of the height. Atmospheric depth, haze, a few strong light sources rising from below. Mood: awe, quiet menace, an invitation to go down. Pathos: the inhabitants are worthy and dangerous enemies — alive, proud, each with a character in the posture — not mannequins, not statues on display. The first two attached images are style references only: take their brushwork, light and color handling, not their subjects or composition. The other attached images are portraits of some of the inhabitants of this place: keep their look — body, material, face, clothing and tools — but paint them small, as full figures standing in the scene at their distance and turned toward the viewer; do not copy the portraits' framing, crop or pose.

Subject: the Workshop of Forms (air, the god Vial), the first hall under Endalor. The place: a hall so huge that its vault is lost in darkness and its walls in haze; here the god once sculpted living beings from clay before giving them to the world above, and the work was left in the middle. Bodies come out of the walls half-sculpted — an arm without a hand, a back without a face, a beast with only one half made. Heavy wooden worktables stand in rows with unfinished clay works, sculpting chisels and clay-stained cloths. Pale sand is everywhere: it lies in drifts between the tables, falls from cracks in the vault in thin streams, and in places stands as a column of falling sand from floor to vault, like an hourglass no one turns. Light: white-green crystals grow in the cracks of the floor and walls and glow from within, like a candle left in each, and throw a cold halo upward; the only warm color in the hall is the ochre clay. The silence of a workshop abandoned in the middle of the day. Nothing is ugly: every body is made precisely and calmly, just not finished. Who waits here, from near to far: (1) in the middle distance, between the worktables, three unfinished elves of grey-green clay stand turned toward the viewer — the Faceless one, a slender elf-shaped figure in a sketch of clothing with a rope for a belt, holding a stone blank of a sword without a guard; his smooth face has only two shallow thumb marks where the eyes should be, and still he looks straight at you; the Long-armed one, thin and stooped, whose one arm reaches almost to the floor and ends in a heavy stone hand; the Hollow one, whose chest is open like an empty mold, his head thrown back, a thin whirl of sand and air leaving his chest; (2) at a table on the right, two servants in clay aprons who still keep working — a thickset apprentice with forearms twice as thick as they should be, kneading a lump of clay, and a tall stooped carver whose right hand is a fan of thin blades — both have raised their heads and look at the viewer; (3) far in the depth, towering over the last tables, the First Sketch — a hunched giant three times the height of a man, made of two halves that do not match: the left half an elf, the right half a beast with clay fur, a clawed paw and a beast's leg; instead of a face a smooth mask with two hollows; a small foreign hand is stuck on his side; he is trying a clay part against his own body; (4) at the very end of the hall, in front of a tall dark passage that glows faintly white-green and leads deeper down, stands the Master — the only finished one: a tall slender elf of smooth polished clay with long hair and a calm face, eyes closed, a master's apron, wrapped forearms, a chisel of glowing white-green stone at his belt, one hand raised palm forward: stop. He is small with distance but clearly readable against the light of the passage. Composition: the path between the worktables leads from the bottom of the picture to the Master and the glowing passage; the First Sketch looms in the haze just before it; columns of falling sand stand on both sides of the path; the left quarter is the near wall in deep shadow with a half-sculpted body emerging from it; the bottom of the picture is dark floor with drifts of sand.

No text, no letters, no numbers, no glyphs, no runes that look like letters, no real-world scripts: tablets, slabs, cylinders, banners and walls carry no writing at all — only blank surfaces or long straight parallel grooves. No watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no border or frame around the picture. No occult symbols, no pentagrams. No gore, no blood, no skulls, no bones, no corpses, no undead, no twisted or distorted creatures, no demons. No purple, no violet, no magenta light. No heroes, no adventurers, no people from the surface world — only the inhabitants of this place. Not a lineup of portraits, no close-up faces, no figure taller than a third of the picture except the giants in the depth. Not a mannequin, not a crash-test dummy, not a marionette on strings: no stiff, passive, awkward or doll-like poses, no dead or empty eyes.

Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG, the same painting as the attached hero portrait. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, deep near-black shadows. Card frames are hand-crafted and worn — dark forged iron, old gold, weathered stone, tarnished silver, carst crystals that glow from within — rich in detail, precious and dramatic. Light tells the story: it comes from below — from glowing crystals, cracks and gems — cold turquoise (#48E5D4) against warm gold and amber (#DDBC7A, #E6A84B); dust motes and sparks float in the light. Dark fantasy: mystery and gravity, high contrast. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime, no flat vector style.

Draw exactly one image in a single pass: no alternative versions, no second attempts, no text in the reply.

Format: a concept sheet for the hero card of a dark fantasy mobile RPG, landscape 16:9. On a plain dark background — near-black slate (#0C0E11) with a soft vignette, no table, no scenery — stand exactly three vertical hero cards side by side in one row, evenly spaced and the same size. Each card is tall and narrow, in a 9:16 proportion, about five sixths of the canvas high, seen straight on, flat, not tilted, not in perspective, fully inside the canvas with a small margin. The three cards show the same hero in the same card design at three steps of power, from left to right: weak, strong, legendary. The player must feel the difference in power at a glance, before reading any number: from left to right the frame grows richer, the light brighter, the aura and the particles stronger. Each card may spill its glow and particles onto the dark background around it.

Attached images, in this order: (1) the hero's portrait; (2) the rarity crystal; (3) a lit rune stone; (4) an unlit rune stone; (5) the valor star; (6) the combat power icon; (7) the class icon. They give the exact look of these elements on the cards; do not copy their plain square backgrounds.

The hero, the same on all three cards: the old dwarf from image 1 — a bald head, a stern furrowed face, a long white braided beard, a heavy brown leather coat studded with iron rivets, a round iron-rimmed shield on his arm, a heavy chain with a huge old iron key across his chest. Keep his face, clothes, colors and pose as in image 1. He is painted edge to edge inside the card's window: head in the upper third, shown down to the hips; the dark stone and amber crystals of his portrait fill the window behind him.

Layout — every card has the same elements in the same places, unless the concept below says otherwise:
- top center: the rarity crystal — the faceted almond-shaped crystal of image 2, set into the top of the frame; one per card;
- right under it, along the top edge of the window: a short arc of valor star places. Each star is the compass star of image 5 without its tile: four long sharp rays in a cross — never a five-pointed star. A filled place is a glowing gold star; an empty place is a dark hollow star-shaped socket;
- top left corner: a small round badge with the level number — digits only, no word such as Level or Lv;
- top right corner: the element medallion — a small round disc, not a hexagon: a rim of dark iron and old gold around a chunk of amber rock glowing from within (Earth, #EB9D40). It is not the class icon;
- the rune stones — tall six-sided stones in gold bezels, pointed at the top and at the bottom, exactly like images 3 and 4, never drop-shaped: a vertical column of three stones along the left edge of the window and a vertical column of only two stones along the right edge; five stones in total, never six;
- bottom: a blank name plaque across the card — smooth, with nothing written on it. Under it one row: the class icon of image 7 on the left — a shield on a hexagonal tile, the only place on the card where this shield icon appears — and the combat power to its right: the crossed swords of image 6 followed by the number.
The digits are clean, bold and legible, in light warm gold.

What each card shows:
- Left card, weak: a milky-white rarity crystal; valor: a single star place — exactly one empty star socket and nothing more, because this hero's maximum is one star; level 34; all five rune stones unlit, dark grey like image 4; combat power 1240.
- Middle card, strong: a violet rarity crystal (#A986EE); THREE star places — two gold stars and one empty socket; level 512; the three rune stones on the left lit with turquoise light like image 3, the two on the right unlit; combat power 48350.
- Right card, legendary: a green rarity crystal (#5FD67A); FIVE star places, all five gold and blazing; level 1200; all five rune stones lit — three on the left, two on the right; combat power 912780.

Concept: Breakout — the power shows as how far the hero outgrows his card: the weaker he is, the tighter the frame holds him; the stronger he is, the further he steps out of it toward the viewer. Left card: a thick plain frame of dark stone and iron around a small window; the hero is small and fully contained inside it, slightly dim. Middle card: the frame is thinner and gilded at its edges, the window larger; the hero is bigger — the rim of his round shield crosses over the frame's left edge and casts a shadow on it; a soft violet glow. Right card: the frame is reduced to a golden base with the name plaque and four golden corners; the hero is much bigger than the window and steps out of the card toward the viewer: his shoulders, his beard and the great round shield spill over the left and right edges of the frame and hide parts of it, and his head comes forward in front of the frame, with the valor stars and the crest still visible above it. Cracks run through the golden corners where he breaks out, stone chips fly, green light erupts from below, embers and dust swirl around him. The crest at the top of every card holds the rarity crystal — white, violet, green — never a rune stone.

No words, no letters, no real-world alphabets, no Roman numerals, no runes, glyphs or markings that look like writing, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no captions, titles or labels above or under the cards. The only characters anywhere in the picture are the digits of the level and combat power numbers given above — no word Level, no Lv, no letters on any badge; the name plaque stays blank. items.prompt:
Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG, the same painting as the attached hero portrait. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, deep near-black shadows. Card frames are hand-crafted and worn — dark forged iron, old gold, bronze, weathered stone, carst crystals that glow from within — rich in detail, precious and dramatic. Light comes from below — from glowing crystals, cracks and gems — cold turquoise (#48E5D4) against warm gold and amber (#DDBC7A, #E6A84B); dust motes and sparks float in the light. Game interface icons on the cards are bold, clean and readable at a small size. Dark fantasy: mystery and gravity, high contrast. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime, no flat vector style.

Draw exactly one image in a single pass: no alternative versions, no second attempts, no text in the reply.

Format: a concept sheet for the hero card of a dark fantasy mobile RPG, landscape 16:9. On a plain dark background — near-black slate (#0C0E11) with a soft vignette, no table, no scenery — stand exactly three vertical hero cards side by side in one row, evenly spaced and the same size. Each card is tall and narrow, in a 9:16 proportion, about five sixths of the canvas high, seen straight on, flat, not tilted, not in perspective, fully inside the canvas with a small margin. The three cards show the same hero with the same card design at three steps of power, from left to right: weak, strong, legendary. The frame grows richer from left to right, and the icons on the card tell the player exactly how strong the hero is. This sheet presents one system of icons: the layout is the same on all three cards, only the states of the icons and the richness of the frame change. Every icon must be easy to read and to count.

The first attached image is the hero's portrait: the old dwarf — a bald head, a stern furrowed face, a long white braided beard, a heavy brown leather coat studded with iron rivets, a round iron-rimmed shield on his arm, a heavy chain with a huge old iron key across his chest. Paint him the same on all three cards, with his face, clothes, colors and pose as in the portrait, edge to edge inside the card's window, head in the upper third, shown down to the hips. The other attached images are our game icons, listed in the concept below; they give the exact look of these elements on the cards; do not copy their plain square backgrounds.

What the three cards must show — the concept below says how:
- rarity: the left card is common — white (#E6E8EA); the middle card is epic — violet (#A986EE); the right card is timeless — green (#5FD67A);
- valor — the hero's personal maximum and how much of it is taken: left — maximum 1, taken 0; middle — maximum 3, taken 2; right — maximum 5, taken 5. There are exactly as many valor places as the maximum, never more;
- rune limits — always exactly five places: left — none passed; middle — three passed; right — all five passed;
- level: 34, 512, 1200; combat power: 1240, 48350, 912780 — digits only, never with a word;
- class: tank — the shield icon; element: Earth — a small round medallion of dark iron and old gold around a chunk of amber rock glowing from within (#EB9D40).
Every card also has a blank name plaque with nothing written on it. The digits are clean, bold and legible, in light warm gold.

Concept: the Crown of Valor. Attached icons after the portrait: (2) the rarity crystal; (3) a lit rune stone; (4) an unlit rune stone; (5) the combat power icon — crossed swords; (6) the class icon — a shield on a hexagonal tile.

Frame — gold filigree. Left card: a plain narrow frame of dull dark bronze with flat edges, no ornament, no glow. Middle card: a gilded frame, delicate filigree scrolls curl out of the four corners, a soft violet glow along the inner edge. Right card: a sumptuous frame of polished old gold with dense openwork filigree along every edge, a warm golden radiance behind the card, embers and gold sparks swirling around it.

Icons and layout:
- Valor is a crown standing on top of the card. Its spikes are the valor places: a taken valor is a spike tipped with a glowing gold gem, an empty place is a spike with an empty dark socket. Left card: a plain low bronze circlet with one single short spike in its middle, its socket empty — no other spikes. Middle card: a gilded crown with exactly three spikes — the left and the middle spike hold glowing gold gems, the right spike holds an empty socket. Right card: a tall ornate golden crown with exactly five spikes, all five tipped with blazing gold gems.
- Rarity: the rarity crystal (image 2) set in the front of the crown's band, under the spikes — white on the left card, violet on the middle card, green on the right card.
- Class and element flank the crown at the top corners of the card: the class icon (image 6) on the left, the element medallion on the right.
- Bottom: the blank name plaque; under it one row: a small round gold seal with the level number on the left and the combat power — the crossed swords (image 5) and the number — on the right.
- Rune limits: five rune stones (images 3 and 4) set in one straight horizontal row into the bottom edge of the frame, under that row. Left card: all five unlit. Middle card: the three on the left lit with turquoise light, the two on the right unlit. Right card: all five lit.

No words, no letters, no real-world alphabets, no Roman numerals, no runes, glyphs or markings that look like writing, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no captions, titles or labels above or under the cards. The only characters anywhere in the picture are the digits of the level and combat power numbers — no word Level, no Lv, no letters on any badge; the name plaque stays blank. No pentagrams, no occult signs, no crosses. No phone mockup, no hands holding the cards, no table, no perspective, no tilted or overlapping cards, no fourth card. The hero has exactly two arms and two hands; no empty eyes.

The first attached image is the hero's portrait: the old dwarf — a bald head, a stern furrowed face, a long white braided beard, a heavy brown leather coat studded with iron rivets, a round iron-rimmed shield on his arm, a heavy chain with a huge old iron key across his chest. - rarity: the left card is common — white (#E6E8EA); the middle card is epic — violet (#A986EE); the right card is timeless — green (#5FD67A);

- level: 34, 512, 1200; combat power: 1240, 48350, 912780 — digits only, never with a word or letters: the combat power is always the crossed-swords icon standing right before its number, with no letters such as CP or BP;
- class: tank — the shield icon; element: Earth — a small round medallion of dark iron and old gold around a chunk of amber rock glowing from within (#EB9D40).

Concept: Casual Minimum — the card face shows only three things, large and simple: the rarity color, the arc of valor stars and the combat power, plus a thin line of five lights for the rune limits. Class, element and level are not on this card at all — no class icon, no element medallion, no level number: they live in the hero's detail screen. Attached icons after the portrait: (2) the rarity crystal; (3) the valor star — use only the star, without its tile: four long sharp rays in a cross, never a five-pointed star; (4) the combat power icon — crossed swords.

Frame — thin gold filigree, restrained, the portrait as large as possible. Left card: a thin plain frame of dull bronze. Middle card: a thin gilded frame with small filigree corners. Right card: a thin frame of polished gold with filigree corners, a golden radiance and a few sparks.

Middle card: three turquoise flames on the left, two dark embers on the right. Right card: five bright flames.
- Bottom: a slim blank name plaque, and under it the combat power, big and bold: the crossed swords (image 4) and the number.

No words, no letters, no real-world alphabets, no Roman numerals, no runes, glyphs or markings that look like writing, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no captions, titles or labels above or under the cards. The only characters anywhere in the picture are the digits of the level and combat power numbers — no word Level, no Lv, no abbreviations such as CP, BP or PWR, no letters on any badge or plate; the name plaque stays blank. No pentagrams, no occult signs, no crosses. No phone mockup, no hands holding the cards, no table, no perspective, no tilted or overlapping cards, no fourth card. The hero has exactly two arms and two hands; no empty eyes.

items.title: Карточка героя, тёмное фэнтези 1: кость и реликварий
items.source: Слова автора 30.09.2026 и идея координатора: рамка из резной кости и тёмного дерева; доблесть — свечи на гребне, зажжённые — взятые; пределы — пять душ-камней в железных клетках; редкость — цвет пламени свечей и камня
items.prompt:
Art style: dark fantasy game art for a mobile RPG — gloomy, heavy, noble and uneasy. Hand-painted digital painting, the same painting as the attached hero portrait: visible confident brush strokes, simplified planes, deep near-black shadows, crisp rim light on edges. A muted, desaturated palette: soot black (#050607, #121518), graphite (#262B31), old blackened iron, yellowed bone, dark wood, weathered stone, tarnished dark bronze. Everything is matte, worn and aged: no bright or polished gold, no gloss, no shiny jewellery, no clean saturated game-UI colors. Light is scarce and precious: the scene is lit only from below — cold turquoise carst light (#48E5D4) rising from cracks and crystals — while the stones, flames and signs on the card glow on their own; everything else sinks into shadow. Ash, dust motes and faint embers drift in the light. A hero's power shows as awe and dread, not as wealth. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime, no cartoon, no flat vector style.

Draw exactly one image in a single pass: no alternative versions, no second attempts, no text in the reply.

Format: a concept sheet for the hero card of a dark fantasy mobile RPG, landscape 16:9. In deep darkness — a near-black background (#050607) with a little drifting ash and a faint cold turquoise glow rising from below the bottom edge; no table, no floor, no scenery — stand exactly three vertical hero cards side by side in one row, evenly spaced and the same size. Each card is tall and narrow, in a 9:16 proportion, about four fifths of the canvas high, seen straight on, flat, not tilted, not in perspective, fully inside the canvas with a margin. The three cards show the same hero with the same card design at three steps of power, from left to right: weak, strong, legendary. From left to right the card grows from humble and dim to ancient and awe-inspiring: the frame becomes heavier and more elaborate, the light from below stronger, the ash and embers denser. This sheet presents one system of icons: the layout is the same on all three cards, only the states of the icons and the weight of the frame change. The icons glow on their own and stay easy to read and to count even in the dark.

The first attached image is the hero's portrait: the old dwarf — a bald head, a stern furrowed face, a long white braided beard, a heavy brown leather coat studded with iron rivets, a round iron-rimmed shield on his arm, a heavy chain with a huge old iron key across his chest. Paint him the same on all three cards, with his face, clothes and pose as in the portrait, inside the card's window, head in the upper third, shown down to the hips — but in the dark key of the card: the background behind him sinks into deep shadow — no pale sky, no snow, no bright background — and the light comes from below, catching his beard, face and shield. The other attached images are our game icons, listed in the concept below; they give the shape of these elements on the cards; paint them in the same dark, matte, aged key as the card, and do not copy their plain square backgrounds.

What the three cards must show — the concept below says how:
- rarity: the left card is common — white (#E6E8EA); the middle card is epic — violet (#A986EE); the right card is timeless — green (#5FD67A);
- valor — the hero's personal maximum and how much of it is taken: left — maximum 1, taken 0; middle — maximum 3, taken 2; right — maximum 5, taken 5. There are exactly as many valor places as the maximum, never more;
- rune limits — always exactly five places: left — none passed; middle — three passed; right — all five passed;
- level: 34, 512, 1200; combat power: 1240, 48350, 912780 — digits only, never with a word or letters: the combat power is always the crossed-swords icon standing right before its number, with no letters such as CP or BP;
- class: tank — the shield icon; element: a small round medallion of dark iron around a raw chunk of amber-orange rock glowing from within (#EB9D40) — a rock, not a planet: no globe, no map, no continents.
Every card also has a blank name plaque with nothing written on it. The digits are clean, bold and legible, in pale old gold or bone color.

Concept: the Bone Reliquary — the card is a narrow shrine that keeps the hero like a relic. Attached icons after the portrait: (2) the rarity crystal; (3) a lit rune stone; (4) an unlit rune stone; (5) the combat power icon — crossed swords; (6) the class icon — a shield on a hexagonal tile.

Frame — carved old yellowed bone and dark wood bound with blackened iron. No skulls, no skeletons: the bone is carved into plain ribs, knots and tracery. Left card: a plain narrow frame of dark worn wood with thin strips of yellowed bone, cracked and sooty, a few iron nails; dim, lit only faintly from below. Middle card: the wood is inlaid with carved bone ribs along both sides, a small pointed bone gable over the window, blackened iron bands; warm candle light. Right card: a tall ancient reliquary — the window under a pointed arch of carved bone tracery, slender bone spires on both sides, heavy blackened iron bands; light pours up from below, ash and embers rise around it; solemn and awe-inspiring.

Icons and layout:
- Rarity: the rarity crystal (image 2) in a blackened iron claw setting at the very top of the frame — pale milky white on the left card, violet on the middle card, green on the right card.
- Valor: right under the crystal, a narrow bone shelf along the top edge of the window with candles standing on it in a row, as many candles as the valor maximum. A taken valor is a lit candle whose flame burns in the rarity color; an empty place is a cold unlit candle with a black wick. Left card: one single unlit candle and nothing more. Middle card: exactly three candles — the left and the middle burn with violet flames (#A986EE), the right one is unlit. Right card: five candles, all burning with green flames (#5FD67A), wax dripping over the shelf.
- Rune limits: five small blackened iron cages in one straight row across the bottom of the window, just above the name plaque, each cage holding one rune stone like images 3 and 4. A passed limit is a stone glowing turquoise inside its cage; an unpassed one is a dull grey stone. Left card: all five stones dull. Middle card: the three on the left glow, the two on the right are dull. Right card: all five glow and their light rises onto the hero.
- Level: digits carved into a small bone tag nailed to the top left corner. Element: the element medallion in the top right corner.
- Bottom: a blank bone name plaque; under it one row on a dark iron plate: the class icon (image 6) on the left and the combat power — the crossed swords (image 5) and the number — on the right.

No words, no letters, no real-world alphabets, no Roman numerals, no runes, glyphs or markings that look like writing, no lines of text on pages, leather or stone, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no captions, titles or labels above or under the cards. The only characters anywhere in the picture are the digits of the level and combat power numbers — no word Level, no Lv, no abbreviations such as CP, BP or PWR, no letters on any badge or plate; the name plaque stays blank. No skulls, no skeletons, no blood, no gore. No pentagrams, no occult signs, no crosses, no religious symbols. No bright polished gold, no glossy plastic shine, no clean bright mobile-game UI look. No phone mockup, no hands holding the cards, no table, no floor, no perspective, no tilted or overlapping cards, no fourth card. The hero has exactly two arms and two hands; no empty eyes.

items.source: Слова автора 30.09.2026 о книжной системе; доблесть — ленты-закладки: по GDD §10.4 каждая доблесть открывает одну главу истории героя
items.prompt:
Art style: dark fantasy game art for a mobile RPG — gloomy, heavy, noble and uneasy. Hand-painted digital painting, the same painting as the attached samples: visible confident brush strokes, simplified planes, deep near-black shadows, crisp rim light on edges. A muted, desaturated palette: soot black (#050607, #121518), graphite (#262B31), old leather, blackened iron, dark bronze, yellowed bone, aged parchment. Everything is matte, worn and aged: no bright or polished gold, no gloss, no shiny jewellery, no clean saturated game-UI colors. Light is scarce and precious: the scene is lit only from below — cold turquoise carst light (#48E5D4) — while the crystals, padlocks, page edges and valor signs glow on their own; everything else sinks into shadow. Ash, dust motes and faint embers drift in the light. A hero's power shows as awe and age, not as wealth. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime, no cartoon, no flat vector style.

Draw exactly one image in a single pass: no alternative versions, no second attempts, no text in the reply.

This is a concept for the hero cards of a dark fantasy mobile RPG in which every hero is a book: tapping the card opens the book, and everything about the hero — skills, growth, the chapters of his story — is a part of that book. The first attached image is the hero's portrait. The second attached image is the approved style sample: take from it the dark painted book covers, the column of five padlocks with their turquoise light, the round level badge, the element medallion, the class shield, the combat power icon and the glow around the book — but none of its red wax seals, cords or rings: there are no wax seals anywhere. The other attached images are our game icons, listed below; they give the shape of these elements; paint them in the same dark, matte, aged key, and do not copy their plain square backgrounds.

The rules of the book system:
- The kind of book is the hero's personal valor maximum, from 1 to 5. The book grows in mass, craft and age, never in gloss: 1 — a small plain book in soft worn brown leather over thin boards, no metal at all; 2 — a sturdier book in dark leather with four iron corner pieces and one leather strap with an iron buckle across its lower part; 3 — a tome in an oklad: the cover framed by plates of dark bronze with engraved borders and bronze bosses at the corners; 4 — a heavy codex: thick boards in black leather bound with iron straps, plates of carved yellowed bone at the corners, large iron bosses; 5 — a grimoire: a massive cover in a rich oklad of blackened iron and carved bone with spiked iron corners, its page edges blazing with light that spills out, ash and embers rising.
- Rarity is the crystal set at the top center of the book plus the color of the glow around the book: common — white (#E6E8EA), almost no glow; rare — yellow (#F0CC4F); unique — turquoise (#1FB8D0); epic — violet (#A986EE); timeless — green (#5FD67A).
- Rune limits are always exactly five small iron padlocks hanging in one vertical column along the right edge of the book. A passed limit is an open padlock, unlocked, with turquoise light (#48E5D4) streaming out of its keyhole; an unpassed one is a closed dark padlock. Passed limits count from the top.
- Valor: the book has exactly as many valor places as its maximum, never more; the concept below says what they look like. A valor sign never looks like a padlock or a crystal.
- Level: digits in a round badge at the top left. Element: a small round medallion of dark iron around a raw chunk of amber-orange rock glowing from within (#EB9D40) — a rock, not a planet — at the top right. Class: the tank's shield icon at the bottom left. Combat power: the crossed-swords icon right before its number, at the bottom right. Digits only — never a word, never letters such as Lv, CP or BP. The digits are clean, bold and legible, in pale old gold.
- The hero, wherever he is painted: the old dwarf of the first attached image — a bald head, a stern furrowed face, a long white braided beard, a heavy brown leather coat studded with iron rivets, a round iron-rimmed shield, a heavy chain with a huge old iron key — the same face, clothes and pose, head in the upper third, shown down to the hips, his background in deep shadow, lit from below; his beard stays white. Under his portrait, a blank name plate with nothing written on it.

Format: a concept sheet, landscape 21:9. On near-black darkness with a faint turquoise glow rising from below — no table, no floor, no scenery — stand exactly five closed books side by side in one row, each seen straight on from the front as a vertical card in a 9:16 proportion, about two thirds of the canvas high, evenly spaced, the same size, flat, not tilted, not in perspective, placed a little above the middle so that the ribbons hanging below them fit in the canvas. From left to right they are the five kinds of book, 1 to 5, with the hero's portrait painted on a panel set into each cover. Attached icons after the style sample: (3) the white crystal — common; (4) the yellow crystal — rare; (5) the turquoise crystal — unique; (6) the violet crystal — epic; (7) the green crystal — timeless; (8) the combat power icon — crossed swords; (9) the class icon — a shield on a hexagonal tile.

Valor in this concept — bookmark ribbons, the chapters of his story that the hero has opened. Flat silk bookmark ribbons hang out of the bottom edge of the book, from under the name plate, and dangle below the book side by side — as many ribbons as the book's valor maximum. A taken valor is a ribbon of the book's rarity color ending in a small metal four-pointed star that glows amber-gold (#E6A84B); an untaken one is a faded, frayed grey ribbon ending in a dull dark metal star. No wax, no seals, no rings, no cords.

The five books, left to right:
1) Book 1, common: a milky-white crystal, almost no glow; valor 0 of 1 — one single faded ribbon and nothing more; padlocks: the top one open and shining, the four below closed; level 34; combat power 1240.
2) Book 2, rare: a yellow crystal and a soft yellow glow; valor 1 of 2 — two ribbons: the left one yellow with a glowing star tip, the right one faded; padlocks: the top two open and shining, the three below closed; level 150; combat power 8420.
3) Book 3, unique: a turquoise crystal and a turquoise glow; valor 2 of 3 — three ribbons: the left two turquoise with glowing star tips, the right one faded; padlocks: the top three open, the two below closed; level 350; combat power 48350.
4) Book 4, epic: a violet crystal and a violet glow; valor 3 of 4 — four ribbons: the left three violet with glowing star tips, the right one faded; padlocks: the top four open, the lowest closed; level 700; combat power 210600.
5) Book 5, timeless: a green crystal and a strong green glow; valor 5 of 5 — five ribbons, all green with glowing star tips; all five padlocks open and shining; level 1200; combat power 912780.

No words, no letters, no real-world alphabets, no Roman numerals, no runes, glyphs or markings that look like writing, no titles or lettering on covers, spines or pages, no handwriting, no lines of text, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no captions or labels. The only characters anywhere in the picture are the digits of the level and combat power numbers — no word Level, no Lv, no abbreviations such as CP, BP or PWR; the name plate stays blank. No wax seals, no seals of any kind, no cords with rings. No skulls, no skeletons, no blood. No pentagrams, no occult signs, no crosses, no religious symbols. No bright polished gold, no glossy plastic shine, no clean bright mobile-game UI look. No phone mockup, no hands, no table, no floor, no tilted books, no perspective. The hero has exactly two arms and two hands; no empty eyes.

This is a concept for the hero cards of a dark fantasy mobile RPG in which every hero is a book: tapping the card opens the book, and everything about the hero — skills, growth, the chapters of his story — is a part of that book. The first attached image is the hero's portrait. The second attached image is the approved style sample: take from it the dark painted book covers, the column of five padlocks with their turquoise light, the round level badge, the element medallion, the class shield, the combat power icon and the glow around the book — but none of its red wax seals, cords or rings: there are no wax seals anywhere. The other attached images are our game icons, listed below; they give the shape of these elements; paint them in the same dark, matte, aged key, and do not copy their plain square backgrounds.

The rules of the book system:
- The kind of book is the hero's personal valor maximum, from 1 to 5. The book grows in mass, craft and age, never in gloss: 1 — a small plain book in soft worn brown leather over thin boards, no metal at all; 2 — a sturdier book in dark leather with four iron corner pieces and one leather strap with an iron buckle across its lower part; 3 — a tome in an oklad: the cover framed by plates of dark bronze with engraved borders and bronze bosses at the corners; 4 — a heavy codex: thick boards in black leather bound with iron straps, plates of carved yellowed bone at the corners, large iron bosses; 5 — a grimoire: a massive cover in a rich oklad of blackened iron and carved bone with spiked iron corners, its page edges blazing with light that spills out, ash and embers rising.
- Rarity is the crystal set at the top center of the book plus the color of the glow around the book: common — white (#E6E8EA), almost no glow; rare — yellow (#F0CC4F); unique — turquoise (#1FB8D0); epic — violet (#A986EE); timeless — green (#5FD67A).
- Rune limits are always exactly five small iron padlocks hanging in one vertical column along the right edge of the book. A passed limit is an open padlock, unlocked, with turquoise light (#48E5D4) streaming out of its keyhole; an unpassed one is a closed dark padlock. Passed limits count from the top.
- Valor: the book has exactly as many valor places as its maximum, never more; the concept below says what they look like. A valor sign never looks like a padlock or a crystal.
- Level: digits in a round badge at the top left. Element: a small round medallion of dark iron around a raw chunk of amber-orange rock glowing from within (#EB9D40) — a rock, not a planet — at the top right. Class: the tank's shield icon at the bottom left. Combat power: the crossed-swords icon right before its number, at the bottom right. Digits only — never a word, never letters such as Lv, CP or BP. The digits are clean, bold and legible, in pale old gold.
- The hero, wherever he is painted: the old dwarf of the first attached image — a bald head, a stern furrowed face, a long white braided beard, a heavy brown leather coat studded with iron rivets, a round iron-rimmed shield, a heavy chain with a huge old iron key — the same face, clothes and pose, head in the upper third, shown down to the hips, his background in deep shadow, lit from below; his beard stays white. Format: a concept sheet, landscape 21:9. items.prompt:
Art style: dark fantasy game UI art for a mobile RPG — gloomy, heavy, noble and uneasy. Hand-painted digital painting: visible confident brush strokes, simplified planes, deep near-black shadows, crisp rim light on the edges. A muted, desaturated palette: soot black (#050607, #121518), graphite (#262B31), blackened iron, old dark leather, dark bronze, yellowed bone, weathered stone. Everything is matte, worn and aged: no bright polished gold, no gloss, no shiny jewellery, no clean saturated game-UI colors. Light is scarce and precious: the frame is lit from below with a crisp rim light along its edges; only its magical parts glow from within. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime, no cartoon, no flat vector style.

Draw exactly one image in a single pass: no alternative versions, no text in the reply.

Format: a frame for a fighter card on the battle screen of a dark fantasy mobile card battler. Landscape 5:4 canvas, seen straight on, flat, not in perspective, perfectly symmetric from left to right. The frame is a landscape rectangle, and its window — the empty opening where the game later puts the fighter's portrait — is a clean landscape rectangle with straight inner edges and small square corners, about 1.35 times as wide as it is tall; the window takes almost the whole frame. Everything on the canvas is solid pure black except the frame itself: the window is pure black and completely empty — no face, no figure, no glow, no smoke, no mist, no reflection, no pattern inside it.

Proportions, strictly: the two side bars and the bottom bar are thin plain bars, each about 3% of the frame width, with no ornament on them; nothing hangs below the bottom bar and nothing sticks out sideways from the lower two thirds of the frame. All ornament gathers on the top bar and at the two top corners: it rises above the top bar by at most one tenth of the frame width and reaches sideways past the side bars by at most one thirtieth of the frame width. Nothing hangs down into the window: the inner edge of the frame is a clean straight line on all four sides.

In the game it is seen very small, about 90 pixels wide: bold, simple, strong silhouettes and one clear accent rather than fine filigree; a thin crisp light rim runs along the inner edge of the frame so that the portrait separates from it. The enemy frames form a ladder of danger: the more dangerous the enemy, the heavier and more terrifying its frame — bone, thorns, horns, dark flame, glowing cracks of carst — awe and dread, never wealth or gloss.

The enemy rank: biome boss — the master of the deepest step of a biome; awe and dread. A heavy frame of blackened iron and old yellowed bone. Two thick curved horns of old bone grow from the top corners and sweep outward and up in low, wide curves; a row of short bone thorns runs along the top bar; at the top center a crown of bone thorns holds a narrow slit of burning ember light (#F0564A fading to #E6A84B), like a half-open watching eye; thin dark smoke curls from the horn tips and stays close to them. The bottom corners are heavy dark iron caps, flat.

The background is solid pure black (#000000), flat, edge to edge: no gradient, no texture, no floor, no cast shadow, no vignette, no checkerboard. Any glow stays close to the frame and fades into the black within a short distance. The whole frame with all its ornament fits inside the central 90% of the canvas: an empty black margin stays on every side — top, bottom, left and right.

No text, no letters, no numbers, no real-world alphabets, no runes or markings that look like writing, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no interface elements other than the frame itself: no buttons, no bars, no gauges, no name plate, no label, no banner with lettering. No skulls, no blood, no gore. No pentagrams, no occult signs, no crosses, no religious symbols. No bright polished gold, no glossy plastic shine. Nothing at all inside the window.

items.source: roster.js c2-01: «Шестьдесят лет давала гудок смен в Стоун-Хейме и ни разу не опоздала. Молодым, уходившим ниже других, говорила: «Дыши, как Хальдур»»; глава «Лишний гудок» (гудок заменяет солнце, три голоса: смена, обед, смена; последняя смена — у рычага). Бил тварей у ворот тем же молотом, которым днём ковал петли для этих ворот»; глава «Петли ворот» («вещь, которую сделал сам, защищаешь сам»; тварь сорвала верхнюю петлю — забил новый штырь тем же молотом под ударами, ровно, как в кузне; остался по ту сторону створки). Решение агента: миг удара — кузнечная кувалда по дуге вправо, из бойка искры и янтарь Земли; за спиной — створка ворот на огромных кованых петлях его работы, верхняя со свежим штырём, ещё красным от жара; кожаный фартук поверх кольчуги; запасные штыри за поясом. Тварей не рисуем. К выгрузке — art/generated/heroes/hero-c2-08-eldgrim__nb2.jpg → design/ui/assets/art/heroes/c2-08.jpg

Subject: Eldgrim Hammer, a dwarf smith of the guild guard, a warrior of great strength of the Earth school. Who he is: by day he forged the hinges for the gate of the dwarven mountain, and when beasts came up from the streams he took the same hammer and went to the gate: a thing you made yourself you defend yourself. Once a beast struck the gate so hard that it tore away the upper hinge; he went outside and drove in a new pin with the same hammer, under the blows, evenly, as at the forge. The gate was closed, and he stayed on the other side. Right now he stands outside the gate and strikes. Character: calm, exact and unstoppable — a craftsman who works under blows as evenly as at his anvil; his brows lowered in concentration, his jaw clenched, his eyes narrowed on the target; he is not angry, he is working. He is short and enormously broad: a barrel chest, a thick short neck, a broad face with a wide nose; in his forties, a shaved head, a thick chestnut beard in two braids singed at the ends, massive scarred forearms. Pose, the moment of the blow: the camera is low; he swings a heavy smith's sledgehammer in a great arc from over his far shoulder down toward the right, his torso twisting into the blow, all his weight behind it. He has exactly two arms: both hands grip the long hammer handle — the near hand high near the head, the far hand at the end of the handle. Sparks and amber-orange light of the Earth school burst from the hammer head. Details that tell his story: (1) the face of the hammer is polished bright by thousands of blows on the anvil; (2) a scorched smith's leather apron over a short mail shirt — forge and war at once; (3) burn scars and forge soot on his forearms; (4) spare iron hinge pins thrust through his belt; (5) behind him, a massive iron-bound gate leaf hung on huge forged hinges of his own work; the top hinge has a fresh pin, still glowing red-hot. Place: outside the narrow gate of a lone dwarven mountain at dusk, the gate shut behind him, dust and sparks in the air. Amber-orange light of the Earth school rises from the cracks below; the red glow of the hot pin.

items.title: Скегги Огнестрел — дворф, физ ДД ловкости, Огонь (c2-09, золото №9, обычная)
items.source: roster.js c2-09: «Стрелок гильдейской дружины. Дворфский огнестрел не прощает спешки, и Скегги не спешил ни разу — даже когда было надо»; глава «Последний заряд» (поторопишься — порох вспыхнет у лица; северяне смеялись, что целится дольше, чем они дерутся; «стреляет поздно, зато один раз»; последний заряд — выждал, пока тварь подойдёт вплотную). Свод: огнестрел и заряды делают только в Стоун-Хейме; твари заводятся у ручьёв. Решение агента: миг выстрела в упор — алое пламя Огня и дым из раструба вправо; огнестрел — длинная тяжёлая ручница: восьмигранный ствол тёмного железа в латунных обручах, раструб, резное ложе, латунная полка у казны; все гнёзда патронташа пусты; Скегги (др.-сканд. «бородатый») — великолепная седая борода в косе, заправленная за пояс подальше от полки; ночь, дорога у ручья, факелы ворот вдали. Тварей не рисуем. К выгрузке — art/generated/heroes/hero-c2-09-skeggi__nb2.jpg → design/ui/assets/art/heroes/c2-09.jpg

Subject: Skeggi Firelock, an old dwarf gunner of the guild guard, a marksman of the Fire school. Who he is: a dwarven gun does not forgive haste — hurry, and the powder flashes in your face. items.title: Ньяль Рудный Меняла — дворф, фармер, без стихии (c2-10, золото №10, обычная)
items.source: roster.js c2-10: «Менял руду на всё, что везли к воротам, и никогда не брал в долг: долга дворф не признаёт»; глава «Без долга» (равным за равное; в долг предлагали под запись у своих судей — отказывал всем; раз в сезон сверял полки с книгой, и книга сходилась; подручному отдал долю за смену вперёд — это мена, не долг). Свод: чужак входит только со сделкой — мена равным за равное; долга и подарка дворф не признаёт. Решение агента: миг сделки — ближняя рука протягивает вправо, чужаку, кусок руды с металлическими жилами, дальняя лежит на закрытой книге с железной застёжкой (надписей не видно); большие латунные весы, чаши ровно; полки с товаром со всего света; кожаный мешочек на краю прилавка — доля подручного вперёд; лупа на шнуре. Без стихии: свет — фонари и отблески литейных, без цвета школы. К выгрузке — art/generated/heroes/hero-c2-10-nyal__nb2.jpg → design/ui/assets/art/heroes/c2-10.jpg

Subject: Nyal the Ore-Changer, a dwarf trader at the gate of the great dwarven mountain, a gatherer of wealth. Art style: dark fantasy game UI art for a mobile RPG — gloomy, heavy, noble and uneasy. Hand-painted digital painting: visible confident brush strokes, simplified planes, deep near-black shadows, crisp rim light on the edges. A muted, desaturated palette: soot black (#050607, #121518), graphite (#262B31), blackened iron, old dark leather, dark bronze, yellowed bone, weathered stone. Everything is matte, worn and aged: no bright polished gold, no gloss, no shiny jewellery, no clean saturated game-UI colors. Light is scarce and precious: the frame is lit from below with a crisp rim light along its edges; only its magical parts glow from within. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime, no cartoon, no flat vector style.

Draw exactly one image in a single pass: no alternative versions, no text in the reply.

Format: a frame for a fighter card on the battle screen of a dark fantasy mobile card battler. Landscape 5:4 canvas, seen straight on, flat, not in perspective, perfectly symmetric from left to right. The frame is a landscape rectangle, and its window — the empty opening where the game later puts the fighter's portrait — is a clean landscape rectangle with straight inner edges and small square corners, about 1.35 times as wide as it is tall; the window takes almost the whole frame. Everything on the canvas is solid pure black except the frame itself: the window is pure black and completely empty — no face, no figure, no glow, no smoke, no mist, no reflection, no pattern inside it.

Proportions, strictly: all four bars are equally slim — the top bar is as slim as the two side bars and the bottom bar, each about 3% of the frame width; the side bars and the bottom bar are plain, with no ornament on them; nothing hangs below the bottom bar and nothing sticks out sideways from the lower two thirds of the frame. All ornament stands on the top bar and at the two top corners: it rises above the top bar by at most one tenth of the frame width; horns and spikes at the top corners grow upward and only a little outward, reaching sideways past the side bars by at most one thirtieth of the frame width. Nothing hangs down into the window: the inner edge of the frame is a clean straight line on all four sides. No smoke, sparks, motes or particles anywhere around the frame.

In the game it is seen very small, about 90 pixels wide: bold, simple, strong silhouettes and one clear accent rather than fine filigree; a thin crisp light rim runs along the inner edge of the frame so that the portrait separates from it. The enemy frames form a ladder of danger: the more dangerous the enemy, the heavier and more terrifying its frame — bone, thorns, horns, dark flame, glowing cracks of carst — awe and dread, never wealth or gloss.

The side: our heroes — one frame for every hero of the player's squad, standing against the enemy. Not a threat: dignity, age and quiet strength, like the binding of an old book of legends. A slim frame of dark leather edged with thin dark bronze lines, bound at the four corners with small blackened iron corner pieces like the corners of an old book cover; a few tiny bronze studs along the bars. At the top center a small round socket of dark bronze set into the top bar, about twice as tall as the bar, empty and pure black inside; nothing else rises above the top bar. Faint cold turquoise carst light (#48E5D4) comes from below and catches the lower corners; everything else is matte and dim. The bars are very slim, like a thin book binding.

The background is solid pure black (#000000), flat, edge to edge: no gradient, no texture, no floor, no cast shadow, no vignette, no checkerboard. Any glow stays close to the frame and fades into the black within a short distance. The whole frame with all its ornament fits inside the central 90% of the canvas: an empty black margin stays on every side — top, bottom, left and right.

No text, no letters, no numbers, no real-world alphabets, no runes or markings that look like writing, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no interface elements other than the frame itself: no buttons, no bars, no gauges, no name plate, no label, no banner with lettering. No skulls, no blood, no gore. No pentagrams, no occult signs, no crosses, no religious symbols. No bright polished gold, no glossy plastic shine. Nothing at all inside the window.

Subject: Grimsa the Horn, an old dwarf woman who for sixty years sounded the shift horn of Stone-Heim, the dwarven city inside a mountain, and was never once late. Subject: Trud the Tincture-Keeper, a dwarf woman, a healer of the mines, with no elemental school: her light is the light of the elven tinctures and her lamp. Who she is: the elves bring tinctures into the mountain, for burns, broken bones and poisoning, and she knew which one heals what, and gave the miners one per shift; more than one only at the alarm horn. Match the brushwork, lighting and color handling of the attached style reference images, but do NOT copy their subjects, objects, letters or composition.

Format: a sheet of square ability icons for a mobile RPG, painted together as one consistent set. The icons stand in a precise grid of equal square cells; the number of columns and rows and the picture in every cell are listed below, row by row from the top, each row from left to right. Between the cells run narrow straight gutters of flat, uniform pure magenta (#FF00FF), and the same magenta gutter runs around the outside of the whole grid. All gutters have the same width, all cells have the same size, and nothing crosses a gutter. Every cell is its own complete square painting filled from edge to edge — the game puts its own frame on top: one clear central image with a bold silhouette that stays readable at 48 px, on a dark near-black stone background with faint cracks and a darker vignette toward the edges of the cell. Light rises from below in the color of the magic school; crisp rim light on the edges of the forms; a few sparks and dust motes in the light. All icons share the same brushwork, lighting, level of detail and palette, so they read as one set, and each icon differs clearly from its neighbours in shape and composition.

The magic school of this sheet is Fire: scarlet fire (#F0564A) with orange and amber flames, glowing embers, grey ash and soot-black stone; the light from below is scarlet and amber. Attacking spells burn a violent, jagged scarlet. Supporting spells — healing, warmth, shields and strength for allies — glow a softer warm gold and amber with rounded, calm shapes. A spell for all targets shows something wide that fills its cell; a spell for two or three targets shows two or three of its thing; a spell for one target shows one focused object. Attacks move to the right, toward the enemies.

The grid: exactly 6 columns and 4 rows, 24 icons.

Row 1: a towering wave of scarlet fire rolling to the right across the ground, filling the whole width, its crest curling over like a breaking sea wave; a bright white-hot spark leaping to the right in a jagged chain of three arcs, a small burst of flame where each arc lands; a funeral pyre of stacked dark logs erupting into one huge column of scarlet flame, sparks spiralling upward; two cupped hands at the bottom releasing a wide, soft fan of warm golden breath full of glowing motes; three small soft golden flames rising like young sprouts from one bed of embers; a dagger blade glowing orange-hot, pressed flat against a strip of white linen bandage, a small puff of steam rising.

Row 2: a huge translucent dome of warm amber flame arched over the dark ground like a protective vault; a circular wall of warm amber flames standing on the stone floor, seen from slightly above, a protective ring around a calm empty centre; a heavy round iron shield wreathed in amber flame, sparks bursting off its rim where a blow has just struck it; a wide low front of creeping scarlet fire spreading across dry grass and ash, many small flames side by side from edge to edge; a flaming torch flying in an arc to the right, trailing fire and dripping burning pitch that lights three small fires below; a charred log burning from within, deep cracks glowing scarlet, three tongues of flame rising from it.

Row 3: a small campfire in a ring of stones seen from the side, its warm golden glow spreading around in soft rings, a few sparks drifting up; three smouldering golden coals nestled in soft grey ash, each with a gentle warm glow and tiny rising motes; a small stone hearth with an iron cooking pot hanging over a steady golden fire, warm light spilling out; thick choking black smoke billowing across the whole cell, scarlet embers smouldering inside it; two dense columns of grey smoke rising from smouldering coals and twisting together into a screen; a single blinding flash of white-hot flame bursting from one point, sharp radiant rays, the centre almost white.

Row 4: grey ash falling like heavy snow over the whole cell, every flake glowing scarlet at its edge; two simple flame-shaped marks smeared in glowing ash on a dark stone surface, as if drawn with a finger; a red-hot branding iron with a simple flame-shaped head glowing scarlet, smoke curling from it; a wide iron brazier with five tall flames rising side by side and leaning together, scarlet and gold, sparks rushing upward; two crossed battle axes whose blades glow orange-hot, flames running along their edges; one sword standing upright, its blade glowing white-hot from hilt to tip, heat shimmer around it.

No text, no letters, no numbers, no captions, titles or labels under, over or inside the icons, no real-world alphabets, no runes or marks that look like writing, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no frames or borders drawn inside the cells. No pentagrams, no occult signs. No magenta or pink anywhere inside the icons: magenta appears only in the gutters.
